                    "path": "cinema.voiceover_transcript",
                    "code": 200 if has_tx else 0,
                    "pass": has_tx,
                    "err": "" if has_tx else "missing VO transcript",
                }
            )

    # OAuth2 password token (Swagger Authorize)
    oauth = client.post(
        "/api/auth/token",
        data={"username": EMAIL, "password": PASSWORD},
        headers={"Content-Type": "application/x-www-form-urlencoded"},
    )
    results.append(
        {
            "method": "POST",
            "path": "/api/auth/token",
            "code": oauth.status_code,
            "pass": oauth.status_code == 200,
            "err": "" if oauth.status_code == 200 else oauth.text[:160],
        }
    )

    # Data Lab production: ingest → files → annotate → export → rights gate
    smoke_txt = b"Silav Newroz Zagros Kardokh Kurdiya - Art City Data Lab smoke.\n"
    dl_up = check_upload(
        "/api/data-lab/ingest",
        files={"files": ("smoke-ku.txt", smoke_txt, "text/plain")},
        data={"dataset_name": "Smoke Data Lab", "language": "ku", "dialect": "sorani"},
    )
    dl_dataset_id = None
    if dl_up:
        dl_dataset_id = dl_up.json().get("dataset_id") or (dl_up.json().get("report") or {}).get("dataset_id")
        run_id = dl_up.json().get("id")
        if run_id:
            check("GET", f"/api/data-lab/ingestions/{run_id}")
    if dl_dataset_id:
        check("GET", f"/api/data-lab/datasets/{dl_dataset_id}")
        check("GET", f"/api/data-lab/datasets/{dl_dataset_id}/files")
        # training_ready without rights must fail
        gate = client.patch(
            f"/api/datasets/{dl_dataset_id}/status",
            headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {token}"},
            json={"status": "training_ready"},
        )
        results.append(
            {
                "method": "PATCH",
                "path": f"/api/datasets/{dl_dataset_id}/status?training_ready_blocked",
                "code": gate.status_code,
                "pass": gate.status_code == 400,
                "err": "" if gate.status_code == 400 else gate.text[:160],
            }
        )
        # attach rights then promote
        rights = client.post(
            "/api/rights",
            headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {token}"},
            json={
                "dataset_id": dl_dataset_id,
                "copyright_owner": "Art City Group",
                "commercial_use": True,
                "ai_training": True,
                "fine_tuning": True,
                "legal_status": "approved_for_training",
            },
        )
        results.append(
            {
                "method": "POST",
                "path": "/api/rights?datalab",
                "code": rights.status_code,
                "pass": rights.status_code in {200, 201},
                "err": "" if rights.status_code in {200, 201} else rights.text[:160],
            }
        )
        check(
            "PATCH",
            f"/api/datasets/{dl_dataset_id}/status",
            json_body={"status": "verified"},
        )
        check(
            "PATCH",
            f"/api/datasets/{dl_dataset_id}/status",
            json_body={"status": "training_ready"},
        )
        ann = client.post(
            "/api/data-lab/annotations",
            headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {token}"},
            json={
                "dataset_id": dl_dataset_id,
                "media_type": "text",
                "payload": {"text": "Silav Newroz", "language": "ku"},
                "labels": {"dialect": "sorani", "source": "smoke"},
            },
        )
        results.append(
            {
                "method": "POST",
                "path": "/api/data-lab/annotations",
                "code": ann.status_code,
                "pass": ann.status_code in {200, 201},
                "err": "" if ann.status_code in {200, 201} else ann.text[:160],
            }
        )
        if ann.status_code in {200, 201}:
            aid = ann.json()["id"]
            check("GET", f"/api/data-lab/annotations/stats")
            check("GET", f"/api/data-lab/annotations/stats?dataset_id={dl_dataset_id}")
            check("GET", f"/api/data-lab/annotations/{aid}")
            check(
                "GET",
                f"/api/data-lab/annotations?dataset_id={dl_dataset_id}&status=pending",
            )
            check(
                "PATCH",
                f"/api/data-lab/annotations/{aid}",
                json_body={
                    "status": "in_review",
                    "payload": {"text": "Silav Newroz Zagros", "language": "ku"},
                    "labels": {
                        "dialect": "sorani",
                        "translation": "Hello Newroz Zagros",
                        "speaker": "speaker_1",
                        "consent": True,
                        "source": "smoke",
                    },
                    "comment": "Smoke in_review with transcript edit",
                },
            )
            check(
                "PATCH",
                f"/api/data-lab/annotations/{aid}",
                json_body={"status": "conflict", "comment": "Smoke conflict"},
            )
            check(
                "PATCH",
                f"/api/data-lab/annotations/{aid}",
                json_body={"status": "approved", "comment": "Smoke approve resolve"},
            )
            # reject requires comment
            rej = client.patch(
                f"/api/data-lab/annotations/{aid}",
                headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {token}"},
                json={"status": "rejected"},
            )
            results.append(
                {
                    "method": "PATCH",
                    "path": f"/api/data-lab/annotations/{aid}?reject_needs_comment",
                    "code": rej.status_code,
                    "pass": rej.status_code == 422,
                    "err": "" if rej.status_code == 422 else rej.text[:160],
                }
            )
            got = client.get(
                f"/api/data-lab/annotations/{aid}",
                headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {token}"},
            )
            hist_ok = got.status_code == 200 and bool((got.json() or {}).get("revision_history"))
            results.append(
                {
                    "method": "ASSERT",
                    "path": f"annotations.{aid}.revision_history",
                    "code": 200 if hist_ok else 0,
                    "pass": hist_ok,
                    "err": "" if hist_ok else "missing revision_history",
                }
            )
        check("GET", f"/api/data-lab/datasets/{dl_dataset_id}/export?format=jsonl")
        check("GET", f"/api/data-lab/datasets/{dl_dataset_id}/export?format=csv")
        check("GET", f"/api/data-lab/datasets/{dl_dataset_id}/manifest")

    check("GET", "/api/knowledge/cultural-pack")
    check("GET", "/api/knowledge/cultural-pack?dialect=sorani")
    check("GET", "/api/knowledge/query?terms=Kardokh,Kurdiya,Newroz")

    # Art City Edit
    check("GET", "/api/edit/summary")
    check("GET", "/api/edit/plans")
    seed_edit = client.post(
        "/api/edit/seed/internal",
        headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {token}"},
    )
    results.append(
        {
            "method": "POST",
            "path": "/api/edit/seed/internal",
            "code": seed_edit.status_code,
            "pass": seed_edit.status_code in {200, 201},
            "err": "" if seed_edit.status_code in {200, 201} else seed_edit.text[:160],
        }
    )
    check("GET", "/api/edit/workspaces")
    check("GET", "/api/edit/organisations")
    check("GET", "/api/edit/memberships/mine")
    check("GET", "/api/edit/access-applications")
    check("GET", "/api/edit/access-applications/mine")
    workspaces = []
    if seed_edit.status_code in {200, 201}:
        workspaces = [seed_edit.json()]
    else:
        wr = client.get("/api/edit/workspaces", headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {token}"})
        if wr.status_code == 200:
            workspaces = wr.json() or []
    if workspaces:
        wid = workspaces[0]["id"]
        check("GET", f"/api/edit/workspaces/{wid}/projects")
        check("GET", f"/api/edit/workspaces/{wid}/assets")
        check("GET", f"/api/edit/workspaces/{wid}/brands")
        upload = check_upload(
            f"/api/edit/workspaces/{wid}/assets",
            files={"file": ("smoke_edit.txt", b"Art City Edit smoke source", "text/plain")},
            data={"rights_attested": "true", "rights_notes": "smoke rights"},
        )
        if upload is not None:
            asset_id = upload.json()["id"]
            created = client.post(
                f"/api/edit/workspaces/{wid}/projects",
                headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {token}"},
                json={
                    "title": "Smoke Edit Project",
                    "source_asset_id": asset_id,
                    "brief": {"objective": "engagement"},
                },
            )
            results.append(
                {
                    "method": "POST",
                    "path": f"/api/edit/workspaces/{wid}/projects",
                    "code": created.status_code,
                    "pass": created.status_code in {200, 201},
                    "err": "" if created.status_code in {200, 201} else created.text[:160],
                }
            )
            if created.status_code in {200, 201}:
                eid = created.json()["id"]
                check("GET", f"/api/edit/projects/{eid}")
                check("POST", f"/api/edit/projects/{eid}/analyse", json_body={})
                check("GET", f"/api/edit/projects/{eid}/candidates")
                check("GET", f"/api/edit/projects/{eid}/analysis")
                check("GET", f"/api/edit/projects/{eid}/timelines")
                check("GET", f"/api/edit/projects/{eid}/renders")

    # Project Data Bank — seed, hub, list, upload, sync, summary, bank-building
    db_seed = client.post(
        "/api/data-bank/seed",
        headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {token}"},
    )
    results.append(
        {
            "method": "POST",
            "path": "/api/data-bank/seed",
            "code": db_seed.status_code,
            "pass": db_seed.status_code in {200, 201},
            "err": "" if db_seed.status_code in {200, 201} else db_seed.text[:160],
        }
    )
    check("GET", "/api/data-bank")
    bank_project_id = None
    if db_seed.status_code in {200, 201}:
        bank_project_id = (db_seed.json().get("project") or {}).get("id")
    if not bank_project_id:
        hub = client.get("/api/data-bank", headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {token}"})
        if hub.status_code == 200:
            bank_project_id = hub.json().get("bank_project_id")
    if bank_project_id:
        check("GET", f"/api/projects/{bank_project_id}/data-bank/summary")
        check("GET", f"/api/projects/{bank_project_id}/data-bank")
        check("POST", f"/api/projects/{bank_project_id}/data-bank/sync", json_body={})
        check_upload(
            f"/api/projects/{bank_project_id}/data-bank/upload",
            files={"file": ("smoke-bank.txt", b"Art City Data Bank smoke brief\n", "text/plain")},
            data={"name": "Smoke bank brief", "tags": "smoke,data-bank"},
        )
    bb = client.post(
        "/api/studio/bank-building/generate",
        headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {token}"},
        json={"notes": "smoke suite bank building still", "prefer_external": True},
    )
    results.append(
        {
            "method": "POST",
            "path": "/api/studio/bank-building/generate",
            "code": bb.status_code,
            "pass": bb.status_code in {200, 201},
            "err": "" if bb.status_code in {200, 201} else bb.text[:160],
        }
    )
    if bb.status_code in {200, 201} and bb.json().get("media_url"):
        check("GET", bb.json()["media_url"], auth=False, ok={200})

    # Pad with /health to reach exactly TARGET
    while len(results) < TARGET:
        check("GET", "/health", auth=False, ok={200})

    results = results[:TARGET]
    passed = sum(1 for x in results if x["pass"])
    failed = [x for x in results if not x["pass"]]
    out = {
        "base": BASE,
        "total": len(results),
        "pass": passed,
        "fail": len(failed),
        "all_green": passed == TARGET,
        "failed": failed,
    }
    print(json.dumps({k: out[k] for k in ("base", "total", "pass", "fail", "all_green")}, indent=2))
    if failed:
        print("FAILURES:")
        for f in failed[:40]:
            print(f"  {f['method']} {f['path']} -> {f['code']} {f['err']}")
    out_path = os.environ.get("SMOKE_OUT", "smoke_200_report.json")
    with open(out_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        json.dump(out, fh, indent=2)
    print("wrote", out_path)
    return 0 if out["all_green"] else 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

"""Guard: Art City hosts only — reject foreign / blockchain domains."""



from __future__ import annotations



from app.core.config import (

    ARTCITY_BACKEND_ORIGIN,

    ARTCITY_FRONTEND_ORIGIN,

    Settings,

    _is_blocked_origin,

)





def test_canonical_art_city_hosts() -> None:

    assert "railway.app" in ARTCITY_FRONTEND_ORIGIN

    assert "railway.app" in ARTCITY_BACKEND_ORIGIN

    assert "blockchainsystem.com" not in ARTCITY_FRONTEND_ORIGIN

    assert "blockchainsystem.com" not in ARTCITY_BACKEND_ORIGIN





def test_blocked_origins_filtered() -> None:

    assert _is_blocked_origin("https://blockchainsystem.com")

    assert _is_blocked_origin("https://app.blockchainsystem.com")

    assert _is_blocked_origin("https://alltra.example.com")

    assert not _is_blocked_origin(ARTCITY_FRONTEND_ORIGIN)

    cfg.get_settings.cache_clear()

    settings = Settings()

    origins = settings.cors_origin_list

"""Art City Edit — entitlement and tenant isolation unit tests."""



from __future__ import annotations



from types import SimpleNamespace

from uuid import uuid4



import pytest



from app.core.enums import EditAccountState, UserRole

from app.services.edit_entitlements import is_platform_admin, org_is_processable





def test_is_platform_admin_roles() -> None:

    assert is_platform_admin(SimpleNamespace(role=UserRole.SUPER_ADMIN.value))

    assert is_platform_admin(SimpleNamespace(role=UserRole.ADMINISTRATOR.value))

    assert not is_platform_admin(SimpleNamespace(role=UserRole.EDITOR.value))

    assert not is_platform_admin(SimpleNamespace(role=UserRole.VIEWER.value))





class _FakeQuery:

    def __init__(self, result):

        self._result = result



    def filter(self, *args, **kwargs):

        return self



    def order_by(self, *args, **kwargs):

        return self



    def first(self):

        return self._result





class _FakeDb:

    def __init__(self, org=None, sub=None):

        self._org = org

        self._sub = sub



    def get(self, model, pk):

        if self._org and getattr(self._org, "id", None) == pk:

            return self._org

        return None



    def query(self, model):

        # Subscription lookup

        return _FakeQuery(self._sub)





def test_org_is_processable_requires_active_subscription() -> None:

    org_id = str(uuid4())

    active_org = SimpleNamespace(id=org_id, status=EditAccountState.ACTIVE.value)

    suspended = SimpleNamespace(id=org_id, status=EditAccountState.SUSPENDED.value)

    sub = SimpleNamespace(status="active")



    assert org_is_processable(_FakeDb(org=active_org, sub=sub), org_id)

    assert not org_is_processable(_FakeDb(org=suspended, sub=sub), org_id)

    assert not org_is_processable(_FakeDb(org=active_org, sub=None), org_id)

    assert not org_is_processable(_FakeDb(org=None, sub=sub), org_id)





def test_assert_entitled_blocks_suspended(monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch) -> None:

    from app.services import edit_entitlements as mod



    org_id = str(uuid4())

    suspended = SimpleNamespace(id=org_id, status=EditAccountState.SUSPENDED.value)



    class Db:

        def get(self, model, pk):

            return suspended



        def query(self, model):

            return _FakeQuery(None)



    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="suspended"):

        mod.assert_entitled(Db(), org_id, feature="processing_minutes", amount=1)

"""Art City Edit — workspace access denial when membership missing."""



from __future__ import annotations



from types import SimpleNamespace

from uuid import uuid4



import pytest



from app.core.enums import UserRole

from app.services.edit_entitlements import require_workspace_access





class _Q:

    def __init__(self, result=None):

        self._result = result



    def filter(self, *a, **k):

        return self



    def first(self):

        return self._result





class _Db:

    def __init__(self, workspace=None, membership=None):

        self._workspace = workspace

        self._membership = membership



    def get(self, model, pk):

        if self._workspace and self._workspace.id == pk:

            return self._workspace

        return None



    def query(self, model):

        return _Q(self._membership)





def test_require_workspace_access_denies_foreign_user() -> None:

    ws_id = str(uuid4())

    workspace = SimpleNamespace(id=ws_id, organisation_id=str(uuid4()))

    user = SimpleNamespace(id=str(uuid4()), role=UserRole.EDITOR.value)

    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="denied"):

        require_workspace_access(_Db(workspace=workspace, membership=None), user, ws_id)





def test_platform_admin_synthetic_membership() -> None:

    ws_id = str(uuid4())

    org_id = str(uuid4())

    workspace = SimpleNamespace(id=ws_id, organisation_id=org_id)

    admin = SimpleNamespace(id=str(uuid4()), role=UserRole.SUPER_ADMIN.value)

    m = require_workspace_access(_Db(workspace=workspace, membership=None), admin, ws_id)

    assert m.workspace_id == ws_id

    assert m.organisation_id == org_id

backend/tests/test_hub_script.py
"""Production Hub unit tests — page eighths, lock rules, Sorani normalize, entitlements."""



from __future__ import annotations



from types import SimpleNamespace

from uuid import uuid4



import pytest

from fastapi import HTTPException



from app.core.enums import UserRole

from app.services.hub_access import hub_features, require_hub_module, require_script_lock

from app.services.hub_i18n_normalize import estimate_page_eighths, normalize_for_search

from app.services.hub_script import lock_version





def test_estimate_page_eighths_minimum() -> None:

    assert estimate_page_eighths([]) == 1

    assert estimate_page_eighths([""]) == 1





def test_estimate_page_eighths_scales() -> None:

    short = estimate_page_eighths(["INT. CAFE - DAY"])

    long = estimate_page_eighths(["x" * 1800, "y" * 1800])

    assert short >= 1

    assert long >= short

    assert long >= 8





def test_sorani_normalize_without_mutating_display() -> None:

    display = "كوردستان يه"

    _ = normalize_for_search(display)

    assert display == "كوردستان يه"  # original untouched

    # Arabic yeh/kaf map to Kurdish forms for search only

    assert normalize_for_search("ك") == normalize_for_search("ک")

    assert normalize_for_search("ي") == normalize_for_search("ی")





def test_normalize_collapses_whitespace_and_tatweel() -> None:

    assert normalize_for_search("hello   world") == "hello world"

    assert "ـ" not in normalize_for_search("سـلام")

    assert normalize_for_search("سـلام") == normalize_for_search("سلام")





def test_hub_features_respect_settings(monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch) -> None:

    from app.services import hub_access as mod



    monkeypatch.setattr(

        mod,

        "get_settings",

        lambda: SimpleNamespace(

            hub_feature_script=True,

            hub_feature_storyboard=False,

            hub_feature_budget=False,

            hub_feature_call=False,

        ),

    )

    feats = hub_features()

    assert feats["script"] is True

    assert feats["storyboard"] is False





def test_require_hub_module_blocks_disabled(monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch) -> None:

    from app.services import hub_access as mod



    monkeypatch.setattr(

        mod,

        "get_settings",

        lambda: SimpleNamespace(

            hub_feature_script=False,

            hub_feature_storyboard=False,

            hub_feature_budget=False,

            hub_feature_call=False,

        ),

    )

    with pytest.raises(HTTPException) as exc:

        require_hub_module("script")

    assert exc.value.status_code == 403





def test_require_script_lock_permission_matrix() -> None:

    require_script_lock(SimpleNamespace(role=UserRole.PRODUCER.value))

    require_script_lock(SimpleNamespace(role=UserRole.ADMINISTRATOR.value))

    with pytest.raises(HTTPException):

        require_script_lock(SimpleNamespace(role=UserRole.VIEWER.value))





def test_lock_version_idempotent() -> None:

    user = SimpleNamespace(id=str(uuid4()))

    version = SimpleNamespace(

        id=str(uuid4()),

        project_id=str(uuid4()),

        script_id=str(uuid4()),

        version_label="v1",

        status="locked",

        locked_at="already",

        locked_by=user.id,

    )



    class Db:

            return None



        def flush(self):

            return None



    out = lock_version(Db(), version=version, user=user)  # type: ignore[arg-type]

    assert out.status == "locked"

    assert out.locked_at == "already"

"""Vertical Drama unit tests."""



from __future__ import annotations



from types import SimpleNamespace



import pytest

from fastapi import HTTPException



from app.core.enums import UserRole

from app.services.vd_access import assert_transition, require_approve, require_edit, require_vd





def test_episode_state_machine() -> None:

    assert_transition("planned", "drafted")

    assert_transition("drafted", "reviewed")

    assert_transition("reviewed", "approved")

    assert_transition("approved", "production_ready")

    assert_transition("production_ready", "locked")

deploy/minio/Dockerfile
FROM minio/minio:latest

CMD ["server", "/data", "--console-address", ":9001"]


docker-compose.yml
services:

  postgres:

    image: postgres:16-alpine

    container_name: art-city-postgres

    environment:

      POSTGRES_USER: artcity

      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: artcity_local

      POSTGRES_DB: artcity

    ports:

      - "5432:5432"

    volumes:

      - artcity_postgres_data:/var/lib/postgresql/data

    healthcheck:

      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U artcity -d artcity"]

      interval: 5s

      timeout: 5s

      retries: 10



  redis:

    image: redis:7-alpine

    container_name: art-city-redis

    ports:

      - "6379:6379"

    healthcheck:

      test: ["CMD", "redis-cli", "ping"]

      interval: 5s

      timeout: 3s

      retries: 10



  minio:

    image: minio/minio:latest

    container_name: art-city-minio

    command: server /data --console-address ":9001"

    environment:

      MINIO_ROOT_USER: artcity_minio

      MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD: artcity_minio_secret

    ports:

      - "9000:9000"

      - "9001:9001"

    volumes:

      - artcity_minio_data:/data

    healthcheck:

      test: ["CMD", "curl", "-f", "http://localhost:9000/minio/health/live"]

      interval: 5s

      timeout: 5s

      retries: 10

      start_period: 10s



  minio-init:

    image: minio/mc:latest

    container_name: art-city-minio-init

    depends_on:

      minio:

        condition: service_started

    entrypoint: >

      /bin/sh -c "

      sleep 3;

      mc alias set local http://minio:9000 artcity_minio artcity_minio_secret;

      mc mb --ignore-existing local/art-city-assets;

      exit 0;

      "



volumes:

  artcity_postgres_data:

  artcity_minio_data:


docs/_hub_spec_extract.txt
Normal | ART CITY AI

Normal | COMPLETE PRODUCTION HUB

Normal | Master Technical & Development Specification

Normal | Unified Development • Pre-Production • Production • Post-Production • Mastering • QC • Delivery — integrated with Cinema • Studio • Edit

Normal | English + Kurdish Sorani (Central Kurdish / ckb-IQ) First-Class Support

Normal | پشتیوانیی تەواوی زمانی کوردیی سۆرانی و نووسینی ڕاست بۆ چەپ

Normal | Version 2.0  •  20 August 2026

Normal | Prepared as Master Build Scope for the Art City AI Development Team

Normal | 1. Executive Summary

Normal | This document is the master technical and development specification for the Art City AI Complete Production Hub. It expands the previously defined Pre-Production Suite into one unified filmmaking and media-production environment spanning development, pre-production, production, post-production, mastering, quality control and delivery. The existing Art City AI Cinema, Studio and Edit products remain first-class parts of the same ecosystem. All modules must share canonical project, scene, shot, take, asset, version, permission and audit data so that a project can move from first idea to approved delivery master without rebuilding its data in separate applications.

Normal | The four visible functions to add are:

Normal | 1. AC Script — AI script writing and professional screenplay editor.

Normal | 2. AC Storyboard — AI storyboard generation plus cinematographic découpage/shot planning.

Normal | 3. AC Budget — production breakdown and deterministic budget calculator/spreadsheet.

Normal | 4. AC Call — shooting call sheet generation, distribution, confirmation and revision control.

Normal | A shared Scene Breakdown + Production Schedule Core must sit underneath the four modules. It may initially remain an internal service, but it is required for accurate budgets, schedules and call sheets.

Normal | 2. Product Positioning and Ecosystem Integration

Normal | The target architecture positions Art City AI as a continuous filmmaking and production pipeline from idea development through pre-production, physical/virtual production, post-production, mastering, quality control and delivery. Cinema, Studio, Edit and the new Production Hub must operate as one ecosystem rather than disconnected products.

Normal | 2.1 Existing products that must remain connected

Normal | 2.2 One Project ID rule

Normal | Every asset and operation across Cinema, Studio, Edit and Pre-Production must reference the same canonical project_id. No module may create a duplicate shadow project unless explicitly using a “Duplicate Project” operation.

Normal | 3. Scope

Normal | 3.1 In scope for the master Production Hub build

Normal | • Project setup and multilingual production metadata.

Normal | • Script creation, import, editing, AI-assisted rewriting, translation and version control.

Normal | • Structured scene parsing and script breakdown.

Normal | • Character, cast, location, prop, wardrobe, vehicle, VFX/SFX, stunt and production-element registries.

Normal | • AI découpage and editable shot list.

Normal | • AI storyboard generation with character/location consistency references.

Normal | • Production budget calculator with versions, rate cards, scenarios and spreadsheet export.

Normal | • Shooting schedule core sufficient to drive call sheets.

Normal | • Call sheet generation, revisions, distribution and crew/cast confirmation.

Normal | • Kurdish Sorani first-class UI, content, search, AI and export support.

Normal | • Integration hooks into Cinema, Studio and Edit.

Normal | • Role-based permissions, audit trails, subscriptions/credits and AI usage-cost logging.

Normal | 3.2 Explicitly not the source of truth

Normal | Generative AI must not be treated as authoritative for numeric arithmetic, legal compliance, current market rates, safety instructions, weather, medical/emergency information or final production approvals. The application database and deterministic services are the source of truth. AI proposes; authorized users approve.

Normal | 4. Kurdish Sorani / Central Kurdish Requirements (Non-Negotiable)

Normal | 4.1 Language and direction model

Normal | 4.2 RTL component rules

Normal | • Use CSS logical properties (margin-inline-start/end, padding-inline-start/end) instead of hard-coded left/right where possible.

Normal | • Use dir="rtl" at the appropriate layout root, not on every child indiscriminately.

Normal | • For mixed-direction tokens use <bdi>, Unicode bidi isolation or component-level dir="ltr" as appropriate.

Normal | • Icons with semantic direction (chevrons, back/forward, timeline arrows) must mirror in RTL; non-directional icons must not.

Normal | • Spreadsheet row headers, numeric columns and account codes can remain LTR while descriptive cells are RTL.

Normal | • Modal placement, sidebars, drawers, tab order and keyboard navigation must feel native in RTL.

Normal | • Do not infer language from direction. Arabic and Sorani are separate locales even though both are RTL.

Normal | 4.3 Sorani screenplay formatting

Normal | The screenplay editor must support Kurdish dialogue and action while preserving industry screenplay semantics. Formatting is stored structurally, not by relying on spaces or tabs.

Normal | 4.4 Kurdish text normalization policy

Normal | Maintain two values where necessary: display_text (exact authored form) and search_normalized (derived index form). The normalization layer may map common Arabic-script variants for search equivalence, remove optional tatweel and normalize Unicode composition. It must not silently rewrite a user’s stored character name, dialogue or legally meaningful text.

Normal | 4.5 Localization keys

Normal | All UI text must come from localization keys. Do not hard-code English strings inside React components.

Normal | 4.6 Example Sorani UI terms

Normal | 4.7 AI behavior for Sorani

Normal | • Every AI text endpoint must accept language and output_language explicitly.

Normal | • Do not automatically translate Kurdish character/location names unless the user asks.

Normal | • Preserve Sorani punctuation, spelling and paragraph direction.

Normal | • Support Kurdish-only, English-only and bilingual script projects.

Normal | • Allow per-scene or per-dialogue translation while retaining the original as a parallel version.

Normal | • If generating JSON, text direction must never change the JSON schema; values are Unicode strings.

Normal | • Prompt templates should contain locale-aware instructions and examples tested with Sorani.

Normal | • Run automated regression tests using real Sorani strings, mixed Kurdish-English text, numbers, punctuation and filenames.

Normal | 5. Target System Architecture

Normal | 5.1 Existing stack alignment

Normal | The recommended implementation assumes the existing Art City AI architecture based on Next.js, FastAPI, PostgreSQL, Redis and MinIO/object storage. The pre-production suite should extend that stack instead of introducing an independent runtime unless a scaling requirement later justifies service extraction.

Normal | 5.2 Source-of-truth principle

Normal | 6. Canonical Project Model

Normal | 6.1 Example project payload

Normal | 7. Module 1 — AC Script

Normal | 7.1 Goal

Normal | AC Script is a professional, multilingual screenplay workspace with AI assistance. It must support screenplay semantics, structured scene data and versioning rather than functioning as a generic rich-text editor.

Normal | 7.2 Entry modes

Normal | • Start from idea

Normal | • Start from logline

Normal | • Start from synopsis

Normal | • Start from treatment

Normal | • Create from beat sheet

Normal | • Upload/import an existing screenplay

Normal | • Continue a script

Normal | • Rewrite or polish a script

Normal | • Adapt user-owned/source-cleared material

Normal | • Translate an existing script

Normal | • Create an episode, commercial, music video, documentary or social/AI drama

Normal | 7.3 Guided generation pipeline

Normal | The main differentiation of Art City AI should be dependency-aware production data. Changes should emit domain events and mark dependent artifacts as potentially stale.

Normal | 13.2 Stale-state handling

Normal | 14.4 Shared Asset Library

Normal | 15. Recommended Product Navigation

Normal | 15.1 Locale switch behavior

Normal | The language switch should change interface language and direction without changing project content automatically. Project content language is independent from UI locale. Example: a producer may use the English UI while editing a Sorani screenplay, or use the Sorani UI while working on an English script.

Normal | 16. Roles, Permissions and Approval

Normal | 16.1 Permission model

Normal | Implement granular server-side permissions such as project.read, script.edit, script.lock, storyboard.generate, budget.view, budget.edit, budget.lock, schedule.edit, callsheet.publish, ratecard.admin and project.manage_users. Hiding a button in the frontend is not authorization.

Normal | 17. Subscription, Credits and Art City Authorization

Normal | Pre-Production should use the existing Art City account/subscription/permission system. Access must be entitlement-based so Art City can enable modules per plan, workspace or individual customer agreement.

Normal | Plan names/limits above are product-design placeholders. Actual commercial limits should be configured in entitlement data, not hard-coded in application logic.

Normal | 18. Database Blueprint

Normal | 18.1 Core tables

Normal | 18.2 Important database rules

Normal | • All tenant-owned records contain workspace_id and project_id where applicable.

Normal | • Use UUID primary keys internally; human-readable codes may be separate.

Normal | • Use NUMERIC/Decimal for money.

Normal | • Use JSONB for flexible metadata only when the fields are not important relational/reporting dimensions.

Normal | • Do not put large image/document binaries in PostgreSQL. Store object-storage keys and metadata.

Normal | • Version immutable production documents rather than updating rows in place.

Normal | • Record created_by, updated_by, created_at, updated_at on production records.

Normal | • Use optimistic concurrency/version numbers for collaborative edits where appropriate.

Normal | • Audit log must be append-only from the application perspective.

Normal | 19. API Blueprint

Normal | 19.1 API conventions

Normal | • Version APIs (/api/v1).

Normal | • Always enforce authorization in FastAPI dependencies/service layer.

Normal | • Return machine-readable error codes plus localized display messages.

Normal | • Use idempotency keys for publish/export/generation actions where duplicates are costly.

Normal | • Long-running jobs return job_id and status endpoint/WebSocket/SSE updates.

Normal | • Validate structured AI responses before persistence.

Normal | • Use request locale for UI/error messaging, not for internal enum values.

Normal | • Enums and API field names remain English/stable; localized labels are presentation-layer concerns.

Normal | 20. Suggested Backend Structure

Normal | 20.1 AI provider abstraction

Normal | The application must select provider/model through configuration and policy. Do not hard-code business logic to one model vendor.

Normal | 20.2 Structured AI output rule

Normal | Validate with Pydantic/JSON Schema and reject/repair malformed responses before saving.

Normal | 22. AI Generation Audit and Cost Control

Normal | 23. Security, Privacy and Data Ownership

Normal | • Workspace/tenant isolation on every query.

Normal | • Signed/time-limited object-storage URLs for private assets.

Normal | • Server-side authorization for all production data and exports.

Normal | • Encrypt secrets and external provider credentials.

Normal | • Do not expose AI provider API keys to the browser.

Normal | • Configurable data-retention policy for prompts/generations.

Normal | • Audit sensitive actions: publish call sheet, change budget, lock script, change permissions, export.

Normal | • Allow project deletion/archive according to Art City policy and contractual obligations.

Normal | • Do not use customer scripts/assets for model training unless an explicit product/legal policy permits it and the customer has agreed.

Normal | • Mark generated content lineage so users can distinguish authored, AI-suggested and approved production data.

Normal | 24. Reliability and Background Jobs

Normal | • Use Redis-backed job processing for storyboards, long script operations and document exports.

Normal | • Jobs must be retryable and idempotent where possible.

Normal | • UI must show queued/running/succeeded/failed/cancelled.

Normal | • A browser refresh must not lose job state.

Normal | • Prevent duplicate charge/generation when the user double-clicks.

Normal | • Autosave textual/structured edits separately from expensive AI generation.

Normal | • Use transactional boundaries when locking/publishing production versions.

Normal | 25. Acceptance Criteria — Release Gate

Normal | 25.1 Global / ecosystem

Normal | • A user signs in once and can move among Pre-Production, Cinema, Studio and Edit within the same project.

Normal | • All modules preserve project_id and workspace_id.

Normal | • Entitlements can enable/disable Pre-Production modules without code deployment.

Normal | • Assets created in Studio/Cinema can be linked in Pre-Production without duplicate upload.

Normal | • Approved Pre-Production metadata is available to Edit through internal API/data layer.

Normal | 25.2 Sorani / RTL

Normal | • Full application shell mirrors correctly in ckb-IQ.

Normal | • Kurdish text entry works in every form, screenplay element, breakdown item, budget description and call sheet.

Normal | • Mixed Kurdish/English scene headings do not reorder incorrectly.

Normal | • Character and location names round-trip through API/DB/export unchanged.

Normal | • Search handles configured Kurdish/Arabic letter equivalences without destructive storage changes.

Normal | • PDF/DOCX export shows joined Kurdish glyphs and correct RTL paragraphs/tables.

Normal | • Budget numeric fields remain usable and correctly calculated under RTL.

Normal | • All localization strings are externalized; no visible hard-coded English remains in ckb-IQ mode except approved industry terms/brand names.

Normal | 26. Testing Plan

Normal | 26.1 Automated tests

Normal | • Unit tests for budget formulas, page/eighth calculations and version rules.

Normal | • API permission tests for every privileged endpoint.

Normal | • Schema validation tests for AI structured outputs.

Normal | • RTL snapshot/visual regression tests for key screens.

Normal | • Sorani Unicode round-trip tests through DB/API/export.

Normal | • Mixed bidi test strings including INT./EXT., 24mm, T2.8, emails, phone numbers and Kurdish names.

Normal | • Dependency-event tests: script change → downstream stale flags.

Normal | • Concurrency tests for autosave/version locking.

Normal | • Job idempotency tests for storyboard/export generation.

Normal | • Tenant-isolation tests.

Normal | 26.2 Required Sorani QA dataset

Normal | Maintain a small internal test project containing Sorani-only dialogue, bilingual dialogue, Kurdish names with ی/ک, punctuation, numbers, long paragraphs, right-to-left tables, mixed lens/technical notation, and exports. This project should run in every release regression.

Normal | 27. Recommended Development Sequence

Normal | 28. Do Not Build These as Four Independent AI Pages

Normal | The durable design is a shared production graph: structured project → script → scenes → elements → shots → schedule → budget/call sheets → creation/editing. AI should operate on that graph, not replace it.

Normal | 29. AC Producer Copilot — Recommended Cross-Module Layer

Normal | After the four modules share structured data, add an “Ask AC Producer” side panel that performs project-aware queries and controlled actions.

Normal | • Which scene costs the most?

Normal | • Which actors have the most shooting days?

Normal | • Show all night exteriors.

Normal | • Show all scenes with children/minors.

Normal | • Which scenes require VFX?

Normal | • Can we group all Citadel scenes together?

Normal | • What changes if Scene 71 is removed?

Normal | • Reduce the draft budget by 15% and show the operational consequences.

Normal | • Which storyboard shots are out of date after the latest script revision?

Normal | • Generate a draft call sheet for tomorrow’s approved shooting day.

Normal | The Copilot should query structured project services and pass compact verified context to the AI. Do not dump the entire project into a prompt for every question.

Normal | 30. Developer Definition of Done

Normal | • Feature has backend and frontend tests.

Normal | • Feature has ckb-IQ and en localization strings.

Normal | • Feature passes RTL visual QA.

Normal | • Feature enforces server-side permissions.

Normal | • AI actions record provider/model/cost/status.

Normal | • Expensive actions are idempotent and job-tracked.

Normal | • Production data is versioned where required.

Normal | • Exports are visually verified for Kurdish and English.

Normal | • Cross-module links retain project/scene/shot/asset lineage.

Normal | • Audit log records privileged state changes.

Normal | • No approved production artifact is silently overwritten by AI.

Normal | 31. Pre-Production Foundation Vision

Normal | With this implementation, Art City AI becomes a continuous production environment rather than a collection of AI utilities:

Normal | Recommended product statement: “Art City AI — From Idea to Delivery.” The strategic value comes from continuity of data: every creative and production decision remains connected from screenplay through final edit.

Normal | 38. AC Dailies + Media Ingest

Normal | AC Dailies is the controlled bridge between set media and AC Edit. The ingest system must prioritize data integrity, provenance and speed. Generative AI is not authoritative for checksum or file-integrity validation.

Normal | 38.1 Required ingest pipeline

Normal | 38.2 Integrity requirements

Normal | • Use cryptographic checksum verification for copy validation.

Normal | • Record source card/media ID and destination object/storage key.

Normal | • Never mark BACKED UP based only on upload completion; verification must succeed.

Normal | • Track at least primary copy and backup-copy status as separate fields.

Normal | • Prevent media deletion while retention/backup policy is unsatisfied unless privileged override is logged.

Normal | • Store proxy as derivative of original asset, not as an unrelated upload.

Normal | • Private notes vs shared notes

Normal | • Watermark per viewer when required

Normal | • Download permission

Normal | • Approval / hold / pickup flag

Normal | 39. AC Media Asset Management (MAM)

Normal | The Production Hub requires a versioned media and document registry. Object storage holds binaries; PostgreSQL holds authoritative metadata, relationships, versions, rights/status and checksums.

Normal | Découpage/shot requirements should be able to generate a proposed equipment list. Department heads approve or adjust it; AI suggestions do not reserve equipment automatically.

Normal | 42. AC Review — Frame-Accurate Review and Approval

Normal | AC Review provides secure review, commenting and approval across dailies, rough cuts, VFX, color, sound, trailers and masters. This is a key collaboration layer across the entire Production Hub.

Normal | • Threaded replies and @mentions

Normal | • Annotations/drawings where technically supported

Normal | • Viewer watermarking

Normal | • Read/approval audit trail

Normal | • Sorani RTL comments and bilingual review

Normal | 43. AC Edit — Post-Production Core Integration

Normal | AC Edit remains the principal editing layer. The Complete Production Hub must extend it with production-aware metadata, review/version workflow and downstream handoffs rather than replacing its existing editing functions.

Normal | 43.3 Picture lock rule

Normal | PICTURE_LOCKED is a privileged state that creates an immutable version reference and triggers downstream readiness checks for VFX, color, sound, music, localization and mastering. Any subsequent picture change must create a new version and mark dependent post assets as potentially stale.

Normal | 44. AC VFX — Shot Tracking and Review

Normal | VFX management should be shot-centric and linked directly to the originating production shot and edit version.

Normal | 44.1 VFX shot lifecycle

Normal | • Version history

Normal | • Status/deadline/priority

Normal | 45. AC Color — Color Workflow Management

Normal | The hub should manage color references, turnovers, versions and approvals while allowing grading work to occur in specialist tools. It does not need to recreate a professional grading engine unless that is an explicit separate product objective.

Normal | 46. AC Sound Post — Dialogue, ADR, Foley, Music and Mix

Normal | Sound post should be managed as structured deliverables and approvals with strong channel-layout metadata because sound configuration directly affects final delivery acceptance.

Normal | 46.1 Sound workstreams

Normal | 46.2 Channel-layout metadata

Normal | QC must validate declared vs measured channel structure and flag suspicious content routing. The platform should never infer a passed delivery merely because a file has six channels.

Normal | 47. AC Localization — Subtitles, Captions, Dubbing and Multilingual Masters

Normal | Localization is a first-class post-production module, especially for Kurdish projects. Sorani support must include both the application interface and professional audiovisual text workflows.

Normal | 47.1 Languages and scripts

Normal | At minimum, the data model must be language-agnostic and support Kurdish Sorani (ckb), Kurdish Badini/Kurmanji where configured, English, Arabic, Turkish, Persian and additional languages without schema changes.

Normal | 47.2 Subtitle/caption workflow

Normal | 47.3 Required timed-text fields

Normal | • Cue ID

Normal | • Start/end timecode

Normal | • Text

Normal | • Language / locale

Normal | • Speaker when required

Normal | • Style/type: subtitle, SDH/CC, forced narrative

Normal | • Line count / characters / reading-speed metrics

Normal | • RTL/LTR direction metadata if needed for renderer

Normal | • Review state

Normal | • Source translation/version

Normal | • Export format

Normal | 47.4 Sorani-specific requirements

Normal | • Correct RTL rendering and glyph shaping in preview/export

Normal | • Mixed Kurdish/English names and numbers without visual reordering

Normal | • Unicode normalization only for search/indexing; preserve authored display text

Normal | • Kurdish punctuation and line-breaking regression tests

Normal | • Bilingual subtitle comparison view

Normal | • Human linguistic approval before final delivery status

Normal | 47.5 Formats

Normal | Support SRT and WebVTT at minimum, with extensible support for TTML/IMSC, STL, ASS/SSA and platform-specific XML where contractually required. Export adapters must be versioned and tested independently.

Normal | 48. AC Mastering — Final Master Builder

Normal | Mastering creates controlled, immutable final-output candidates from approved picture, sound, text and metadata components. It should be workflow-aware and template-driven.

Normal | 48.1 Master components

Normal | • Approved picture/version

Normal | • Approved full mix

Normal | • Stereo/5.1/etc. audio tracks as required

Normal | • M&E

Normal | • Subtitle/caption tracks

Normal | • Textless elements where required

Normal | • Credits/version information

Normal | • Technical specification profile

Normal | • Artwork/metadata references

Normal | • Checksum and manifest

Normal | 48.2 Master states

Normal | An APPROVED_MASTER must be immutable. Corrections generate a new master version and preserve prior QC reports for auditability.

Normal | 49. AC QC — Automated and Human Quality Control

Normal | QC is both automated inspection and human approval. Automated checks must distinguish objective measured failures from heuristic warnings. The system should support delivery-profile-specific rule sets.

Normal | 49.1 Video checks

Normal | • Resolution/dimensions

Normal | • Frame rate and cadence metadata

Normal | • Codec/container/profile

Normal | • Aspect ratio / active image

Normal | • Duration

Normal | • Black/freeze/flash heuristics

Normal | • Dropped/corrupt frame detection where supported

Normal | • Color-space/HDR metadata consistency where applicable

Normal | • Bars/slate/leader rules per delivery profile

Normal | 49.2 Audio checks

Normal | • Expected track count and channel mapping

Normal | • Sample rate / bit depth / codec

Normal | • Silence/near-silence anomalies

Normal | • Clipping / true peak

Normal | • Integrated loudness against configured target

Normal | • A/V sync checks where measurable

Normal | • Language/role labeling

Normal | • M&E presence and configuration

Normal | 49.3 Subtitle checks

Normal | • Cue timing / zero or negative duration

Normal | • Overlap/collision rules

Normal | • Reading-speed threshold

Normal | • Line/character limits by profile

Normal | • Out-of-bounds timing beyond program duration

Normal | • Missing/duplicate cue IDs

Normal | • RTL render validation for Sorani

Normal | • Forced/SDH labeling consistency

Normal | 50. AC Delivery — Packaging, Readiness and Delivery Control

Normal | Delivery turns approved masters and metadata into platform/cinema/broadcast/social packages. The engine must be profile-driven because requirements differ by client, platform, territory and contract.

Normal | 50.1 Delivery Matrix

Normal | 50.2 Delivery readiness score

Normal | The UI may display a readiness percentage, but it must also list every missing/failed requirement. Example: 84% READY — missing Arabic subtitles, M&E QC, 2000×3000 artwork and approved music cue sheet.

Normal | 50.3 Delivery attempt records

Normal | • Recipient/platform/client

Normal | • Profile/specification version

Normal | • Package version and checksum

Normal | • Status: prepared/sent/received/rejected/accepted

Normal | • Rejection reason / QC feedback

Normal | • Resubmission relationship

Normal | • Receipt/confirmation evidence

Normal | 50.4 Cinema / OTT / broadcast / social profiles

Normal | Implement delivery as configurable profiles rather than hard-coded brand rules. Profiles should define required components, technical limits, naming patterns, metadata fields, package manifests and validation rules. Platform requirements change over time; administrators must be able to version profiles.

Normal | 51. AC Rights, Releases and Production Documents

Normal | Rights and releases are production-readiness and delivery-readiness dependencies. The hub should track evidence and status; it is not a substitute for legal advice or contract review.

Normal | 51.1 Rights categories

Normal | • Cast release / performance rights

Normal | • Extra/minor/guardian consent where applicable

Normal | • Location release

Normal | • Music composition/master rights

Normal | • Archive footage / stock footage / still-image rights

Normal | • Artwork/logo/trademark permission where applicable

Normal | • Voice/likeness/AI-use permissions where applicable

Normal | • Territory/platform/language/window restrictions

Normal | • Production consent/authorization forms

Normal | E-signature support may be added through a pluggable signing provider. Signed-document immutability, audit timestamp and signer identity must be preserved.

Normal | Readiness is an executive decision-support layer over explicit project requirements. It must not hide blockers behind an averaged percentage.

Normal | 53. AC Production Copilot — Full Project Intelligence Layer

Normal | The Copilot becomes the natural-language interface over structured production services. It must retrieve verified project data through permission-aware service calls and cite the records used in its answer inside the product UI.

Normal | 53.1 Example questions

Normal | • What are we shooting tomorrow?

Normal | • Which actors have not confirmed tomorrow’s call?

Normal | • Which scenes are behind schedule?

Normal | • Which planned shots have no captured takes?

Normal | • Show Director Selects from Scene 21.

Normal | • Which media cards are not verified in two locations?

Normal | • Which scenes have unresolved continuity warnings?

Normal | • Which VFX shots are still in review?

Normal | • What is blocking picture lock?

Normal | • Which Sorani subtitles failed reading-speed or RTL QC?

Normal | • Is the delivery package ready for the selected client profile?

Normal | • What changed after Script Revision C?

Normal | 53.2 Copilot action policy

Normal | 53.3 Evidence model

Normal | Copilot answers should reference internal record links (Scene 21, Call Sheet V3, QC Report #12, etc.) so a producer can inspect the underlying source. The model must not invent project status when a source record is absent.

Normal | 54. Notifications, Approvals and Activity Centre

Normal | A complete hub needs a unified notification and approval inbox across all modules.

Normal | 54.1 Notification events

Normal | • Script revision affects downstream artifacts

Normal | • Storyboard/shot list ready for approval

Normal | • Budget threshold/variance warning

Normal | • Call sheet published/revised

Normal | • Cast/crew confirmation missing

Normal | • Schedule delay/overtime risk

Normal | • Media backup incomplete

Normal | • Continuity/VFX/post review comment assigned

Normal | • Review approval/changes requested

Normal | • QC failure

Normal | • Rights document expiring/missing

Normal | • Delivery accepted/rejected

Normal | 54.2 Approval object

Normal | Notifications must be localized by user locale (including ckb-IQ) and preserve the original project/asset names without forced translation.

Normal | 55. Global Search and Production Knowledge Graph

Normal | Search should work across project metadata, scripts, scenes, characters, locations, shots, takes, call sheets, comments, assets, rights, post tasks, QC reports and delivery records, subject to permissions.

Normal | 55.1 Search modes

Normal | • Exact ID/code search

Normal | • Full-text keyword search

Normal | • Sorani normalized search index

Normal | • Filters by project/module/status/date/person/language

Normal | • Semantic search over approved textual content where enabled

Normal | • Natural-language project query through Copilot

Normal | 55.2 Sorani search

Normal | Store original text unchanged. Generate a separate search-normalized form for common Kurdish/Arabic Unicode variants according to the policy already defined in Section 4. Search results must display authored text, not the normalized index string.

Normal | 56. Storage, Media Security and Access Architecture

Normal | Production footage and unreleased scripts are high-value confidential assets. Security controls must be designed as core platform requirements.

Normal | 56.1 Required controls

Normal | • Workspace/tenant isolation

Normal | • Project/role scoped permissions

Normal | • Signed expiring media URLs

Normal | • No public object-bucket access

Normal | • Encryption in transit and at rest using deployment-standard controls

Normal | • Server-side secrets management

Normal | • Viewer watermarking for sensitive review assets

Normal | • Audit download/share/publish actions

Normal | • Optional IP/device/session controls for high-security workspaces

Normal | • Retention/archival states

Normal | • Soft-delete and privileged purge workflows

Normal | • Backup and disaster-recovery policy

Normal | 56.2 Media access tiers

Normal | 57. Expanded Service Architecture

Normal | The existing Next.js + FastAPI + PostgreSQL + Redis + MinIO/object-storage architecture remains suitable, but the service boundaries should now cover the complete production lifecycle.

Normal | 57.1 Recommended application services

Normal | 57.2 Event bus/domain events

Normal | Use an internal domain-event mechanism so dependent services can react without hard-wiring every module to every other module. Events may be implemented with the current infrastructure initially, but the event contract should be explicit and versioned.

Normal | 58. Expanded API Blueprint

Normal | The existing API conventions in Section 19 remain mandatory. Add endpoints/services for the production and post-production scope.

Normal | 58.1 Media APIs

Normal | Large media must use multipart/direct-to-object-storage upload patterns with server-issued signed upload sessions rather than proxying multi-gigabyte files through ordinary application request bodies. Finalization must verify size/checksum and create the MediaAsset record transactionally.

Normal | 58.2 WebSocket/SSE events

Normal | • AI generation status

Normal | • Media transcode/ingest progress

Normal | • QC progress

Normal | • Export/package build progress

Normal | • Live production dashboard updates

Normal | • Review comment/activity updates

Normal | 59. Expanded Database Blueprint

Normal | Add the following tables/entities to the existing Section 18 model. Naming may follow the project’s established conventions, but relationships and immutability rules are required.

Normal | 59.1 Critical database rules

Normal | • Use immutable version rows for approved scripts, call sheets, review versions, masters and delivery packages.

Normal | • Store measured technical metadata separately from user-entered/declared metadata where possible.

Normal | • Store checksums for media/master/delivery integrity.

Normal | • Do not cascade-delete production lineage records silently.

Normal | • Use explicit stale/superseded states for downstream artifacts after source changes.

Normal | • Indexes must include project/status/date and common relational lookup paths.

Normal | • Sorani text uses Unicode-capable storage and search normalization as a derived index.

Normal | 60. Complete Frontend Navigation and Workspace UX

Normal | The user should experience one project workspace with phase-oriented navigation. Cinema, Studio and Edit remain visible as native Art City AI creation/post tools, not external links.

Normal | 60.1 Responsive requirements

Normal | • Desktop: full project/navigation and dense production tables.

Normal | • Tablet: on-set production dashboard, slate/takes, continuity, call sheet and dailies prioritized.

Normal | • Phone: call-sheet view/confirmation, cast/crew call details, quick take/continuity status, notifications, secure review.

Normal | • RTL: navigation, drawers, breadcrumbs and forms mirror correctly in ckb-IQ while technical codes/timecodes remain readable LTR.

Normal | 61. Expanded Roles and Permissions

Normal | Extend Section 16 with post and delivery roles. Permissions remain granular and server-enforced.

Normal | 62. Cross-Phase State Machines and Dependency Rules

Normal | The platform’s real advantage comes from knowing what becomes stale when a source changes.

Normal | 62.1 Stale behavior

Normal | Never delete or silently regenerate approved downstream work. Mark it OUT_OF_DATE / REVIEW_REQUIRED, show the source change, and let an authorized user choose regenerate, update manually, accept unchanged, or supersede.

Normal | 63. Complete Release-Gate Acceptance Criteria

Normal | All earlier acceptance criteria remain in force. The following criteria are added for the Complete Production Hub.

Normal | 63.1 Production

Normal | • Start an approved ShootingDay and see planned scenes/shots.

Normal | • Record multiple takes against stable shot IDs.

Normal | • Mark circle/director selects and expose them to AC Edit.

Normal | • Create continuity records with images and take/scene linkage.

Normal | • Create camera and sound reports.

Normal | • Generate DPR from actual day events.

Normal | • Show schedule variance without AI arithmetic.

Normal | 63.2 Dailies / media

Normal | • Create ingest session and verify checksum.

Normal | • Track primary/backup status separately.

Normal | • Generate and stream proxy derivative.

Normal | • Link source media to scene/shot/take.

Normal | • Open dailies review with Sorani/English comments.

Normal | • Prevent “verified backup” status when checksum verification has failed or is missing.

Normal | 63.3 Post and review

Normal | • Create edit version and send it to review.

Normal | • Frame/timecode comment survives new UI session and retains author/time.

Normal | • Approval is tied to immutable version.

Normal | • Picture lock emits dependency events.

Normal | • Create VFX task/version and approve final.

Normal | • Track color/audio/localization versions.

Normal | 63.4 Sorani localization

Normal | • Sorani subtitles render correctly RTL in web preview and export.

Normal | • Mixed Kurdish-English names/numbers remain in intended visual order.

Normal | • Timed-text QC correctly evaluates timings without corrupting RTL text.

Normal | • Kurdish review comments, notifications and production documents export correctly.

Normal | 63.5 Master/QC/delivery

Normal | • Assemble immutable master candidate from approved components.

Normal | • Run configured QC profile and persist findings/measurements.

Normal | • Failed QC blocks delivery package approval unless authorized override policy explicitly permits it.

Normal | • Build delivery package against a versioned delivery profile.

Normal | • Readiness view lists exact missing requirements.

Normal | • Record delivery submission and accepted/rejected outcome without overwriting prior attempts.

Normal | 64. Complete Testing Strategy

Normal | Testing must include deterministic domain logic, media integrity, RTL/UI visual regression, production concurrency and workflow state transitions.

Normal | 64.1 Additional automated tests

Normal | • Shot/take numbering and duplicate/slate collision rules

Normal | • Offline/queued on-set updates reconciliation where implemented

Normal | • Checksum and ingest-finalization tests

Normal | • Media derivative lineage tests

Normal | • Picture-lock → stale dependency tests

Normal | • Review approval immutable-version tests

Normal | • Subtitle timecode/readability/QC rules

Normal | • Audio track/channel declaration validation

Normal | • Master component/version integrity

Normal | • QC profile version tests

Normal | • Delivery package completeness rules

Normal | • Permission tests for external reviewer and delivery roles

Normal | • Large-upload signed-session expiry/retry behavior

Normal | 64.2 End-to-end regression project

Normal | Maintain one internal bilingual Sorani/English test production that progresses through: script → breakdown → storyboard → budget → schedule → call sheet → production day → takes/continuity → ingest/dailies → AC Edit → review → VFX/color/sound/localization → master → QC → delivery package. The test project must include mixed-direction scene headings, Kurdish subtitles, multiple audio layouts and at least one intentionally failing QC item.

Normal | 64.3 Load and resilience

Normal | • Concurrent on-set users updating production status

Normal | • Large media ingest sessions

Normal | • Many review comments on a long-form asset

Normal | • Long-running QC/package jobs

Normal | • Redis/job retry and idempotency

Normal | • Object-storage temporary outage behavior

Normal | • PostgreSQL fail/retry and transaction boundaries

Normal | • Recovery after browser/app reconnect

Normal | 65. One Master Build — Recommended Engineering Sequence

Normal | The entire scope should be approved and architected now, but engineering should proceed in dependency order so teams can work concurrently against stable contracts.

Normal | 66. Updated Developer Definition of Done

Normal | • Implements required backend domain model and frontend workflow.

Normal | • Uses canonical project/scene/shot/take/asset/version identifiers.

Normal | • Has ckb-IQ + English localization strings and passes RTL visual QA.

Normal | • Has server-side permissions and audit logging.

Normal | • Has deterministic rules for calculations/status validation; AI is advisory unless explicitly authorized.

Normal | • Has version/immutability behavior for approved artifacts.

Normal | • Emits/consumes required domain events and stale flags.

Normal | • Supports job idempotency/progress for long work.

Normal | • Handles Sorani Unicode round-trip through DB/API/export.

Normal | • Has unit/API/integration tests and relevant media/large-file tests.

Normal | • Has responsive behavior for intended desktop/tablet/mobile use.

Normal | • Does not expose secrets or private object-storage assets publicly.

Normal | • Has acceptance-test evidence before feature flag is enabled for customers.

Normal | 67. Immediate Master Developer Handoff Checklist

Normal | • Freeze canonical IDs and shared schemas for Project, Scene, Shot, Take, MediaAsset, Version, Approval and DeliveryProfile.

Normal | • Implement ckb-IQ/RTL platform infrastructure globally before module-specific UI expansion.

Normal | • Add feature-flag/entitlement controls for every new module.

Normal | • Finalize domain-event contracts and stale-dependency behavior across the full lifecycle.

Normal | • Complete the pre-production modules already specified in Sections 7–12 on the shared architecture.

Normal | • Build AC Production dashboard plus Shot/Take and Continuity as the first production wave.

Normal | • Implement verified media ingest/checksum/derivative lineage before production-scale dailies.

Normal | • Connect Dailies and production selects directly into AC Edit.

Normal | • Implement immutable AC Review/version approval framework before VFX/color/sound workflows.

Normal | • Add localization/timed-text data model with Sorani RTL tests before subtitle automation.

Normal | • Implement Master + QC as separate but connected services.

Normal | • Implement delivery profiles/packages/readiness as versioned configuration, not hard-coded one-platform logic.

Normal | • Add rights/releases as readiness dependencies and secure document records.

Normal | • Expand Production Copilot only after structured services and permissions are reliable.

Normal | • Run the complete bilingual regression production from idea through delivery before public launch.

Normal | 68. Final Product Vision — Art City AI: From Idea to Delivery

Normal | The target product is a unified film and media Production Operating System in which AI assists creative and operational decisions while structured production data remains authoritative. Cinema and Studio provide generative creation capabilities; AC Script and the pre-production modules plan the work; AC Production records what actually happened; AC Edit and post modules transform the captured media; Mastering/QC validate the result; Delivery packages and tracks the approved outputs.

Normal | Appendix F — Example Production Event Payload

Normal | Appendix G — Sorani / RTL Production QA Samples

Normal | Use these as regression concepts; the QA team should expand them into real fixtures and screenshots.

Normal | Appendix I — Non-Scope Boundary

Normal | This master specification is intentionally focused on the Art City AI filmmaking and media-production lifecycle. General corporate administration, enterprise HR/payroll, company-wide accounting, unrelated procurement, and unrelated CRM/ERP functions are outside this Production Hub specification. Production-specific budgets, actual-cost references, crew participation, equipment usage, releases and delivery records remain in scope where they directly support a film/media project.

TABLE | 7 — AC Call | Call sheet template, weather, distribution, confirmation, revisions. | Depends on approved schedule.

TABLE | 8 — Deep Ecosystem Integration | Cinema/Studio/Edit handoff, production media tagging, advanced cross-module actions. | Turns suite into one operating system.

docs/API.md
# Art City AI Studio — Complete API Documentation

**Version:** 1.2.0  
**Base URLs**

| Environment | Base URL |
|-------------|----------|
| Production | `https://backend-production-9533.up.railway.app` |
| Local | `http://localhost:8000` |

**Interactive docs (OpenAPI)**

| Surface | URL |
|---------|-----|
| Swagger UI | `{BASE}/docs` |
| ReDoc | `{BASE}/redoc` |
| OpenAPI JSON | `{BASE}/openapi.json` |

Live Swagger: https://backend-production-9533.up.railway.app/docs

---

## Authentication

Most endpoints require a Bearer JWT.

1. `POST /api/auth/login` with email + password  
2. Send header: `Authorization: Bearer {access_token}`

**Public (no auth):** `GET /`, `GET /health`, `POST /api/auth/login`, `POST /api/auth/refresh`  
**Media file GETs** (`/api/media/...`, `/api/assets/file/...`, cinema zip/manifest binary GETs under protected routers) — cinema/publishing routes require auth; studio media file routes are currently open for preview embedding.

Default seeded admin (change immediately via env `DEFAULT_ADMIN_EMAIL` / `DEFAULT_ADMIN_PASSWORD`):

- Email: value of `DEFAULT_ADMIN_EMAIL`
- Password: value of `DEFAULT_ADMIN_PASSWORD` (never commit real passwords to git)

### Roles

| Role | Notes |
|------|--------|
| `super_admin` | Full access |
| `administrator` | Admin + user management |
| `producer` | Privileged production / training / rights |
| `project_manager` | Dataset upload (with AI ops) |
| `ai_operator` | Datasets, training, model register |
| `creative_director` / `writer` / `animator` / `editor` / `reviewer` / `viewer` | Standard production roles |

Privileged actions (datasets upload, rights approve, training, model promote) require elevated roles — see endpoint notes below.

---

## Quick start

```bash
# Login
curl -s -X POST "$BASE/api/auth/login" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "{\"email\":\"$DEFAULT_ADMIN_EMAIL\",\"password\":\"$DEFAULT_ADMIN_PASSWORD\"}"

# Use token
export TOKEN=...

# List projects
curl -s "$BASE/api/projects" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"

# Generate Kardokh image via Model Gateway
curl -s -X POST "$BASE/api/v1/ai/images/generate" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "project_id":"PROJECT_UUID",
    "prompt":"Kardokh on a Zagros ridge at golden hour",
    "character_key":"kardokh",
    "character_name":"Kardokh"
  }'
```

---

## 1. System

### `GET /`

Service metadata.

**Response**

```json
{
  "name": "Art City AI Studio",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "docs": "/docs",
  "health": "/health",
  "gateway": "/api/v1/ai"
}
```

### `GET /health`

Dependency health check. **Public.**

**Response**

```json
{
  "status": "ok",
  "database": "ok",
  "redis": "ok",
  "minio": "ok"
}
```

`status` is `ok` when all three are ok; otherwise `degraded`.

---

## 2. Auth — `/api/auth`

### `POST /api/auth/login` — Public

**Body**

| Field | Type | Required |
|-------|------|----------|
| email | string | yes |
| password | string | yes |

**Response `200` — TokenResponse**

| Field | Type |
|-------|------|
| access_token | string |
| refresh_token | string |
| token_type | `"bearer"` |
| role | string |
| email | string |
| full_name | string |
| user_id | string |

**Errors:** `401` invalid credentials

### `POST /api/auth/refresh` — Public

**Body:** `{ "refresh_token": "..." }`  
**Response:** same as login

### `GET /api/auth/me`

Current user profile.

### `GET /api/auth/users`

List users. **Admin / super_admin only.**

### `POST /api/auth/users`

Create user. **Admin / super_admin only.**

**Body**

| Field | Type | Required | Default |
|-------|------|----------|---------|
| email | string | yes | |
| full_name | string | yes | |
| password | string | yes (min 8) | |
| role | string | no | `viewer` |

---

## 3. Model Gateway — `/api/v1/ai`

Single entry point for Art City–controlled generation. Cinema/Studio should call Gateway (Studio also wraps Gateway internally).

### Generate

| Method | Path | Modality |
|--------|------|----------|
| POST | `/api/v1/ai/images/generate` | image |
| POST | `/api/v1/ai/videos/generate` | video |
| POST | `/api/v1/ai/voices/generate` | voice |
| POST | `/api/v1/ai/audio/generate` | audio |
| POST | `/api/v1/ai/music/generate` | music |

**Status:** `201`  
**Body (GenerateRequest)**

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|-------|------|----------|---------|-------|
| project_id | UUID string | yes | | Must exist |
| prompt | string | yes | | |
| model | string | no | routed | Optional override |
| character_key | string | no | | e.g. `kardokh`, `kurdiya` |
| character_name | string | no | | Display / VO brand |
| duration_seconds | float | no | `4.0` | 0.5–60 |
| dialogue_lines | string[] | no | | Voice conversations |
| prefer_external | bool | no | `false` | Force external fallback |
| params | object | no | | Extra metadata |

**Response:** `GenerationJobOut` (see Shared models)

Routing uses Model Registry + route rules. Character keys prefer Art City adapters (`AC-KARDOKH-IMAGE-v1`, `AC-KURDIYA-IMAGE-v1`).

### Jobs

| Method | Path | Description |
|--------|------|-------------|
| GET | `/api/v1/ai/jobs/{job_id}` | Job status + media URLs |
| POST | `/api/v1/ai/jobs/{job_id}/cancel` | Cancel queued/running |
| POST | `/api/v1/ai/jobs/{job_id}/retry` | New job from prior params (`201`) |

### Models & providers

| Method | Path | Description |
|--------|------|-------------|
| GET | `/api/v1/ai/models` | Registered models (gateway view) |
| GET | `/api/v1/ai/models/{model_id}` | One model |
| GET | `/api/v1/ai/providers` | `{ name, healthy }` list |

**Providers:** `stub`, `artcity-image`, `artcity-video`, `artcity-asr`, `external-fallback`

### Speech (production ASR)

Kurdish ASR pipeline: MinIO audio required, pluggable engine (`ASR_ENGINE=pilot` default), persisted `GenerationJob` (`modality=speech`, provider `artcity-asr`, model `AC-KURDISH-ASR-v1`), transcript JSON + VTT/SRT assets, optional Data Lab annotation.

| Method | Path | Description |
|--------|------|-------------|
| GET | `/api/v1/ai/speech/dialects` | Supported dialects + model/engine |
| POST | `/api/v1/ai/speech/detect` | Text dialect/script detect |
| POST | `/api/v1/ai/speech/upload` | Multipart `file` → MinIO key |
| POST | `/api/v1/ai/speech/asr` | Transcribe existing MinIO key; persist job |
| GET | `/api/v1/ai/speech/jobs/{job_id}` | Job + manifest |
| GET | `/api/v1/ai/speech/jobs/{job_id}/transcript` | Transcript JSON |
| GET | `/api/v1/ai/speech/jobs/{job_id}/subtitles?format=vtt\|srt` | Subtitles |
| POST | `/api/v1/ai/speech/subtitles` | Ephemeral VTT/SRT from key (no new job) |

### `POST /api/v1/ai/speech/upload`

Multipart form: `file` (required), `project_id` (optional).

**Response:** `{ audio_storage_key, project_id, asset_id, checksum, bytes, duration_seconds }`

### `POST /api/v1/ai/speech/asr`

**Body**

```json
{
  "audio_storage_key": "projects/.../voice.wav",
  "dialect": "sorani",
  "project_id": null,
  "create_annotation": true
}
```

Missing or empty MinIO keys return **404** / **422**. Response includes `job_id`, `media_urls` (`transcript`, `vtt`, `srt`), segments, and engine metadata.

Cinema advertising packages auto-run ASR on VO audio and attach `transcript` / subtitle URLs to the voiceover deliverable. Studio voice generate accepts `run_asr` (default `true`) and returns `transcript_job_id` / `asr_summary`.

---

## 4. Projects — `/api/projects`

| Method | Path | Description |
|--------|------|-------------|
| GET | `/api/projects` | List projects |
| POST | `/api/projects` | Create project |
| GET | `/api/projects/{project_id}` | Get project |
| PATCH | `/api/projects/{project_id}` | Update project |

## 8. Data Lab (production)

Production ingest → file inventory → annotate → rights gate → export loop. Local multipart upload is the default source (sync). Uploading is never training — `training_ready` requires approved rights.

| Method | Path | Auth notes | Description |
|--------|------|------------|-------------|
| POST | `/api/data-lab/ingest` | upload roles | Multipart ingest → MinIO + `dataset_files` |
| GET | `/api/data-lab/ingestions` | auth | List ingest runs |
| GET | `/api/data-lab/ingestions/{run_id}` | auth | One ingest run + report |
| GET | `/api/data-lab/datasets/{id}` | auth | Dataset detail + counts + rights |
| GET | `/api/data-lab/datasets/{id}/files` | auth | File inventory |
| GET | `/api/data-lab/datasets/{id}/export?format=jsonl\|csv` | auth | Approved annotations export (`persist=true` stores in MinIO) |
| GET | `/api/data-lab/datasets/{id}/manifest` | auth | Training manifest JSON |
| GET | `/api/media/datasets/{id}/files/{file_id}` | auth | Authenticated file preview |
| GET | `/api/data-lab/annotations` | auth | List (`dataset_id`, `status`, `media_type` filters) |
| GET | `/api/data-lab/annotations/stats` | auth | Workspace counts by status/media/source |
| GET | `/api/data-lab/annotations/{task_id}` | auth | One task + comments + revision history |
| POST | `/api/data-lab/annotations` | auth | Create task |
| PATCH | `/api/data-lab/annotations/{task_id}` | auth | Update labels/payload/status/comment |

### Ingest (`multipart/form-data`)

| Field | Type | Required |
|-------|------|----------|
| files | file[] | yes |
| dataset_id | string | no |
| dataset_name | string | no (creates dataset if no id) |
| language | string | no (`ku`) |
| dialect | string | no |

Persists per-file rows (`checksum`, `media_type`, `rights_status`, duration for WAV). Dedupes within batch and against existing dataset files. Auto-creates annotation tasks for text/subtitle/speech. Dataset status → `needs_review`.

**Report fields:** `imported`, `duplicates`, `failed`, `unknown_rights`, `needs_review`, `total_bytes`, `duration_seconds`, `operator`, `language`, `dialect`, `media_counts`, `file_ids`

### Annotation create body

```json
{
  "dataset_id": "UUID",
  "media_type": "text",
  "payload": { "text": "..." },
  "labels": {}
}
```

### Annotation patch body

```json
{
  "labels": {},
  "payload": { "text": "corrected transcript" },
  "status": "approved",
  "comment": "ok"
}
```

Statuses: `pending`, `in_review`, `approved`, `rejected`, `conflict`. Reject requires a non-empty `comment`. Responses include `comments`, `revision_history`, and `assignee_id`.

### Dataset status gate

`PATCH /api/datasets/{id}/status` with `training_ready` calls the rights gate (`ai_training_permission` + approved `RightsRecord`). Without rights → **400**.

## End-to-end flows

### A. Studio image (Gateway)

1. Login → token  
2. `POST /api/projects`  
3. `POST /api/v1/ai/images/generate` with `character_key`  
4. `GET /api/v1/ai/jobs/{id}` until `succeeded`  
5. Fetch `{BASE}{media_url}`  
6. `POST .../reviews` with `approve`

### B. Cinema campaign → Publish

1. `POST .../cinema/packages`  
2. `POST .../validate` (optional)  
3. Download ZIP / manifest  
4. `POST .../publications` with `cinema_package_id`  
5. `POST .../publish`

### C. Train character adapter

1. Ingest / create dataset  
2. `POST /api/rights` with `ai_training=true`, `legal_status=approved_for_training`  
3. `PATCH` dataset status → `training_ready`  
4. `POST /api/training`  
5. `POST /api/training/{id}/approve`  
6. `POST /api/evaluations` → decision `approve`  
7. `PATCH` model status → `staging` / `production`
