33. Master Production Hub Scope and Operating Principle



This section expands the earlier Pre-Production specification into the complete Art City AI Production Hub. Everything defined in Sections 1–32 remains part of the master scope unless explicitly superseded below.



33.1 Complete module map



33.2 Single production graph



Stable IDs and lineage are mandatory. A media file imported during production must be traceable back to project → shooting day → scene → shot → take, and a final master must be traceable forward from those source records through edit, post, QC and delivery.



34. AC Production — Live Production Command Centre



AC Production is the operational command centre used while the project is actively shooting. It converts the approved schedule, call sheet, shot list and breakdown into live status and feeds actual results back into the project graph.



34.1 Users



• Producer / Executive Producer



• Director



• 1st Assistant Director



• Production Manager / Coordinator



• Script Supervisor



• Director of Photography / Camera team



• Sound team



• DIT / Data Manager



• Department heads with scoped permissions



34.2 Live dashboard



34.3 Scene state machine



All state changes must be timestamped and attributed. AI may recommend a state or identify risk, but only authorized users may finalize production-status changes.



34.4 Production timeline events



• Crew call actual



• First setup ready



• First shot



• Meal start/end



• Company move start/end



• Scene start/end



• Actor wrap



• Camera wrap



• Production wrap



• Incident or delay event



• Weather interruption



• Equipment failure



• Unplanned overtime trigger



35. AC Slate + Shot / Take Tracker



This module bridges the planned shot list and the footage actually captured. It should be usable on tablet/phone on set and remain functional under unstable connectivity with offline queue/synchronization where practical.



35.1 Take schema



35.2 Take ratings



• NG / False start



• Technical issue



• Performance hold



• Good



• Circle take



• Director select



• Editor select



• Pickup required



35.3 AC Edit handoff



AC Edit must receive shot/take metadata, select flags, scene/shot order, script references, continuity notes and linked proxy/original media. The editor should be able to filter instantly for Director Selects, Circle Takes, missing shots and pickups.



36. AC Continuity — Script Supervisor Workspace



AC Continuity manages script changes and visual/action continuity during shooting. The data must be scene-aware and take-aware rather than stored as free-form daily notes only.



36.1 Continuity categories



• Costume / wardrobe state



• Hair and makeup



• Props and prop position



• Food/drink levels



• Actor blocking and body/hand position



• Eyelines and screen direction



• Vehicle position/damage/state



• Blood, dirt, wetness, injuries and practical effects



• Dialogue changes / ad-libs



• Action changes



• Scene timing



• Camera axis / coverage notes



• Continuity reference photos



36.2 AI-assisted continuity



AI may compare approved continuity reference images and metadata and flag possible mismatches. It must label findings as POSSIBLE CONTINUITY ISSUE and provide the source frames/records. Human confirmation is mandatory; the system must not silently alter continuity records.



37. Camera, Sound and Department Reports



Production metadata must not depend on handwritten reports that are later retyped. Art City AI should provide structured digital reports with exportable PDF/CSV and links to media assets.



37.1 Camera report



• Camera body / serial or unit ID



• Card/reel/media ID



• Clip filename



• Scene / shot / take



• FPS / shutter / resolution / codec



• Lens / focal length / filtration



• LUT / look reference



• Timecode



• Technical notes



• Good/NG/Select status



• Media offload and checksum state



37.2 Sound report



• Recorder / media ID



• Audio filename / roll



• Scene / shot / take



• Timecode



• Track names and channel assignments



• Sample rate / bit depth



• Mic/source notes



• Wild tracks / room tone



• Technical/continuity notes



• Sync status



37.3 Department quick reports



Art, wardrobe, makeup, locations, VFX and SFX departments should have lightweight forms for scene completion, continuity state, consumed materials, special notes, damage/incident flags and next-day preparation.



38. AC Dailies + Media Ingest



AC Dailies is the controlled bridge between set media and AC Edit. The ingest system must prioritize data integrity, provenance and speed. Generative AI is not authoritative for checksum or file-integrity validation.



38.1 Required ingest pipeline



38.2 Integrity requirements



• Use cryptographic checksum verification for copy validation.



• Record source card/media ID and destination object/storage key.



• Never mark BACKED UP based only on upload completion; verification must succeed.



• Track at least primary copy and backup-copy status as separate fields.



• Prevent media deletion while retention/backup policy is unsatisfied unless privileged override is logged.



• Store proxy as derivative of original asset, not as an unrelated upload.



38.3 Dailies review features



• Secure streaming proxy



• Burn-in overlays configurable by role



• Scene/shot/take navigation



• Favourites / Director Select



• Frame/timecode comments



• Private notes vs shared notes



• Watermark per viewer when required



• Download permission



• Approval / hold / pickup flag



39. AC Media Asset Management (MAM)



The Production Hub requires a versioned media and document registry. Object storage holds binaries; PostgreSQL holds authoritative metadata, relationships, versions, rights/status and checksums.



39.1 Asset types



39.2 Asset schema essentials



39.3 Naming convention



Provide a configurable canonical naming policy. Example: PROJECT-SCENE-SHOT-TAKE-CAMERA-DATE-VERSION. The system must preserve the original filename separately and must not rely on filename parsing as the sole source of truth.



40. AC Daily Production Report (DPR)



At wrap, Art City AI should generate a structured Daily Production Report from actual production events rather than asking the production office to rebuild the day manually.



40.1 DPR sections



• Production day/date/location



• Crew call / first shot / meal / last shot / wrap



• Scenes scheduled / completed / partial / moved



• Pages planned vs completed



• Cast worked and wrap times



• Extras and special participants



• Equipment / vehicles / special resources



• Weather summary from verified source



• Incidents / delays / damage



• Overtime



• Media cards/rolls and ingest/backup summary



• Notes for next shooting day



• Authorized sign-off



40.2 Planned vs actual



The example is illustrative only. Actual values are derived from project records. Cost impacts must use the deterministic budget/cost engine and configured rates.



41. Production Crew, Cast and Equipment Operations



The hub needs production-specific people and equipment records to drive schedules, call sheets, permissions and on-set status. This is not a general corporate HR system.



41.1 Production participant object



• Person / contact identity



• Production role and department



• Character/cast relationship if applicable



• Project availability



• Production day calls and actual work times



• Production documents/releases status



• Emergency contact visibility governed by permissions



• Communication preference



• Project-specific rate/reference only where authorized



• Portal/account invitation status



41.2 Equipment operations



Découpage/shot requirements should be able to generate a proposed equipment list. Department heads approve or adjust it; AI suggestions do not reserve equipment automatically.



42. AC Review — Frame-Accurate Review and Approval



AC Review provides secure review, commenting and approval across dailies, rough cuts, VFX, color, sound, trailers and masters. This is a key collaboration layer across the entire Production Hub.



42.1 Core features



• Frame/timecode-accurate comments



• Threaded replies and @mentions



• Annotations/drawings where technically supported



• Version selector and side-by-side/overlay comparison where appropriate



• Approval / changes requested / rejected / locked states



• Private comments by permission



• Secure external review link



• Expiry, passcode and download controls



• Viewer watermarking



• Read/approval audit trail



• Sorani RTL comments and bilingual review



42.2 Review state machine



43. AC Edit — Post-Production Core Integration



AC Edit remains the principal editing layer. The Complete Production Hub must extend it with production-aware metadata, review/version workflow and downstream handoffs rather than replacing its existing editing functions.



43.1 Inputs AC Edit should receive automatically



• Locked/active script version



• Scene and shot IDs



• Découpage/shot order



• Director selects and circle takes



• Camera/sound metadata



• Continuity notes and script changes



• Synced proxies and original-media lineage



• Music/graphic/reference assets from Studio/Cinema



• Deliverable aspect-ratio targets



• Rights/status flags for restricted media



43.2 Edit version object



43.3 Picture lock rule



PICTURE_LOCKED is a privileged state that creates an immutable version reference and triggers downstream readiness checks for VFX, color, sound, music, localization and mastering. Any subsequent picture change must create a new version and mark dependent post assets as potentially stale.



44. AC VFX — Shot Tracking and Review



VFX management should be shot-centric and linked directly to the originating production shot and edit version.



44.1 VFX shot lifecycle



44.2 VFX shot fields



• VFX shot code



• Scene/shot/take linkage



• Plate/source asset



• Edit in/out/timecode reference



• Task/type: cleanup, comp, key, tracking, CG, sky, screen, etc.



• Vendor/artist assignment



• Brief and reference files



• Target resolution/color pipeline



• Version history



• Review comments



• Status/deadline/priority



• Final render asset and checksum



Script Breakdown and Storyboard may flag potential VFX shots early, but VFX production records are created/approved by authorized users.



45. AC Color — Color Workflow Management



The hub should manage color references, turnovers, versions and approvals while allowing grading work to occur in specialist tools. It does not need to recreate a professional grading engine unless that is an explicit separate product objective.



45.1 Required records



• Camera color metadata / log/gamut



• On-set LUT/look reference



• Approved creative look references



• Color turnover asset/version



• Conform status



• Grade version and reviewer



• Display/master target (e.g., SDR/HDR when supported)



• Review/approval status



• Final graded master lineage



46. AC Sound Post — Dialogue, ADR, Foley, Music and Mix



Sound post should be managed as structured deliverables and approvals with strong channel-layout metadata because sound configuration directly affects final delivery acceptance.



46.1 Sound workstreams



46.2 Channel-layout metadata



QC must validate declared vs measured channel structure and flag suspicious content routing. The platform should never infer a passed delivery merely because a file has six channels.



47. AC Localization — Subtitles, Captions, Dubbing and Multilingual Masters



Localization is a first-class post-production module, especially for Kurdish projects. Sorani support must include both the application interface and professional audiovisual text workflows.



47.1 Languages and scripts



At minimum, the data model must be language-agnostic and support Kurdish Sorani (ckb), Kurdish Badini/Kurmanji where configured, English, Arabic, Turkish, Persian and additional languages without schema changes.



47.2 Subtitle/caption workflow



47.3 Required timed-text fields



• Cue ID



• Start/end timecode



• Text



• Language / locale



• Speaker when required



• Style/type: subtitle, SDH/CC, forced narrative



• Line count / characters / reading-speed metrics



• RTL/LTR direction metadata if needed for renderer



• Review state



• Source translation/version



• Export format



47.4 Sorani-specific requirements



• Correct RTL rendering and glyph shaping in preview/export



• Mixed Kurdish/English names and numbers without visual reordering



• Unicode normalization only for search/indexing; preserve authored display text



• Kurdish punctuation and line-breaking regression tests



• Bilingual subtitle comparison view



• Human linguistic approval before final delivery status



47.5 Formats



Support SRT and WebVTT at minimum, with extensible support for TTML/IMSC, STL, ASS/SSA and platform-specific XML where contractually required. Export adapters must be versioned and tested independently.



48. AC Mastering — Final Master Builder



Mastering creates controlled, immutable final-output candidates from approved picture, sound, text and metadata components. It should be workflow-aware and template-driven.



48.1 Master components



• Approved picture/version



• Approved full mix



• Stereo/5.1/etc. audio tracks as required



• M&E



• Subtitle/caption tracks



• Textless elements where required



• Credits/version information



• Technical specification profile



• Artwork/metadata references



• Checksum and manifest



48.2 Master states



An APPROVED_MASTER must be immutable. Corrections generate a new master version and preserve prior QC reports for auditability.



49. AC QC — Automated and Human Quality Control



QC is both automated inspection and human approval. Automated checks must distinguish objective measured failures from heuristic warnings. The system should support delivery-profile-specific rule sets.



49.1 Video checks



• Resolution/dimensions



• Frame rate and cadence metadata



• Codec/container/profile



• Aspect ratio / active image



• Duration



• Black/freeze/flash heuristics



• Dropped/corrupt frame detection where supported



• Color-space/HDR metadata consistency where applicable



• Bars/slate/leader rules per delivery profile



49.2 Audio checks



• Expected track count and channel mapping



• Sample rate / bit depth / codec



• Silence/near-silence anomalies



• Clipping / true peak



• Integrated loudness against configured target



• A/V sync checks where measurable



• Language/role labeling



• M&E presence and configuration



49.3 Subtitle checks



• Cue timing / zero or negative duration



• Overlap/collision rules



• Reading-speed threshold



• Line/character limits by profile



• Out-of-bounds timing beyond program duration



• Missing/duplicate cue IDs



• RTL render validation for Sorani



• Forced/SDH labeling consistency



49.4 QC result model



50. AC Delivery — Packaging, Readiness and Delivery Control



Delivery turns approved masters and metadata into platform/cinema/broadcast/social packages. The engine must be profile-driven because requirements differ by client, platform, territory and contract.



50.1 Delivery Matrix



50.2 Delivery readiness score



The UI may display a readiness percentage, but it must also list every missing/failed requirement. Example: 84% READY — missing Arabic subtitles, M&E QC, 2000×3000 artwork and approved music cue sheet.



50.3 Delivery attempt records



• Recipient/platform/client



• Profile/specification version



• Package version and checksum



• Method / endpoint / transfer reference



• Submitted by / date



• Status: prepared/sent/received/rejected/accepted



• Rejection reason / QC feedback



• Resubmission relationship



• Receipt/confirmation evidence



50.4 Cinema / OTT / broadcast / social profiles



Implement delivery as configurable profiles rather than hard-coded brand rules. Profiles should define required components, technical limits, naming patterns, metadata fields, package manifests and validation rules. Platform requirements change over time; administrators must be able to version profiles.



51. AC Rights, Releases and Production Documents



Rights and releases are production-readiness and delivery-readiness dependencies. The hub should track evidence and status; it is not a substitute for legal advice or contract review.



51.1 Rights categories



• Script/story rights



• Writer/director/producer agreements



• Cast release / performance rights



• Extra/minor/guardian consent where applicable



• Location release



• Music composition/master rights



• Archive footage / stock footage / still-image rights



• Artwork/logo/trademark permission where applicable



• Voice/likeness/AI-use permissions where applicable



• Territory/platform/language/window restrictions



51.2 Rights object



51.3 Production forms



• Cast/extra release



• Location release



• Crew deal memo/production acknowledgement



• NDA/confidentiality document



• Equipment checkout/return



• Vehicle request/use form



• Incident report



• Expense/petty-cash reference if enabled in project



• Production consent/authorization forms



• Call-sheet acknowledgement



E-signature support may be added through a pluggable signing provider. Signed-document immutability, audit timestamp and signer identity must be preserved.



52. Production and Post Readiness Scores



Readiness is an executive decision-support layer over explicit project requirements. It must not hide blockers behind an averaged percentage.



52.1 Production Readiness



52.2 Post / Delivery Readiness



53. AC Production Copilot — Full Project Intelligence Layer



The Copilot becomes the natural-language interface over structured production services. It must retrieve verified project data through permission-aware service calls and cite the records used in its answer inside the product UI.



53.1 Example questions



• What are we shooting tomorrow?



• Which actors have not confirmed tomorrow’s call?



• Which scenes are behind schedule?



• Which planned shots have no captured takes?



• Show Director Selects from Scene 21.



• Which media cards are not verified in two locations?



• Which scenes have unresolved continuity warnings?



• Which VFX shots are still in review?



• What is blocking picture lock?



• Which Sorani subtitles failed reading-speed or RTL QC?



• Is the delivery package ready for the selected client profile?



• What changed after Script Revision C?



53.2 Copilot action policy



53.3 Evidence model



Copilot answers should reference internal record links (Scene 21, Call Sheet V3, QC Report #12, etc.) so a producer can inspect the underlying source. The model must not invent project status when a source record is absent.



54. Notifications, Approvals and Activity Centre



A complete hub needs a unified notification and approval inbox across all modules.



54.1 Notification events



• Script revision affects downstream artifacts



• Storyboard/shot list ready for approval



• Budget threshold/variance warning



• Call sheet published/revised



• Cast/crew confirmation missing



• Schedule delay/overtime risk



• Media backup incomplete



• Continuity/VFX/post review comment assigned



• Review approval/changes requested



• QC failure



• Rights document expiring/missing



• Delivery accepted/rejected



54.2 Approval object



Notifications must be localized by user locale (including ckb-IQ) and preserve the original project/asset names without forced translation.



55. Global Search and Production Knowledge Graph



Search should work across project metadata, scripts, scenes, characters, locations, shots, takes, call sheets, comments, assets, rights, post tasks, QC reports and delivery records, subject to permissions.



55.1 Search modes



• Exact ID/code search



• Full-text keyword search



• Sorani normalized search index



• Filters by project/module/status/date/person/language



• Semantic search over approved textual content where enabled



• Natural-language project query through Copilot



55.2 Sorani search



Store original text unchanged. Generate a separate search-normalized form for common Kurdish/Arabic Unicode variants according to the policy already defined in Section 4. Search results must display authored text, not the normalized index string.



56. Storage, Media Security and Access Architecture



Production footage and unreleased scripts are high-value confidential assets. Security controls must be designed as core platform requirements.



56.1 Required controls



• Workspace/tenant isolation



• Project/role scoped permissions



• Signed expiring media URLs



• No public object-bucket access



• Encryption in transit and at rest using deployment-standard controls



• Server-side secrets management



• Viewer watermarking for sensitive review assets



• Audit download/share/publish actions



• Optional IP/device/session controls for high-security workspaces



• Retention/archival states



• Soft-delete and privileged purge workflows



• Backup and disaster-recovery policy



56.2 Media access tiers



57. Expanded Service Architecture



The existing Next.js + FastAPI + PostgreSQL + Redis + MinIO/object-storage architecture remains suitable, but the service boundaries should now cover the complete production lifecycle.



57.1 Recommended application services



57.2 Event bus/domain events



Use an internal domain-event mechanism so dependent services can react without hard-wiring every module to every other module. Events may be implemented with the current infrastructure initially, but the event contract should be explicit and versioned.



58. Expanded API Blueprint



The existing API conventions in Section 19 remain mandatory. Add endpoints/services for the production and post-production scope.



58.1 Media APIs



Large media must use multipart/direct-to-object-storage upload patterns with server-issued signed upload sessions rather than proxying multi-gigabyte files through ordinary application request bodies. Finalization must verify size/checksum and create the MediaAsset record transactionally.



58.2 WebSocket/SSE events



• AI generation status



• Media transcode/ingest progress



• QC progress



• Export/package build progress



• Live production dashboard updates



• Review comment/activity updates



59. Expanded Database Blueprint



Add the following tables/entities to the existing Section 18 model. Naming may follow the project’s established conventions, but relationships and immutability rules are required.



59.1 Critical database rules



• Use immutable version rows for approved scripts, call sheets, review versions, masters and delivery packages.



• Store measured technical metadata separately from user-entered/declared metadata where possible.



• Store checksums for media/master/delivery integrity.



• Do not cascade-delete production lineage records silently.



• Use explicit stale/superseded states for downstream artifacts after source changes.



• Indexes must include project/status/date and common relational lookup paths.



• Sorani text uses Unicode-capable storage and search normalization as a derived index.



60. Complete Frontend Navigation and Workspace UX



The user should experience one project workspace with phase-oriented navigation. Cinema, Studio and Edit remain visible as native Art City AI creation/post tools, not external links.



60.1 Responsive requirements



• Desktop: full project/navigation and dense production tables.



• Tablet: on-set production dashboard, slate/takes, continuity, call sheet and dailies prioritized.



• Phone: call-sheet view/confirmation, cast/crew call details, quick take/continuity status, notifications, secure review.



• RTL: navigation, drawers, breadcrumbs and forms mirror correctly in ckb-IQ while technical codes/timecodes remain readable LTR.



61. Expanded Roles and Permissions



Extend Section 16 with post and delivery roles. Permissions remain granular and server-enforced.



62. Cross-Phase State Machines and Dependency Rules



The platform’s real advantage comes from knowing what becomes stale when a source changes.



62.1 Stale behavior



Never delete or silently regenerate approved downstream work. Mark it OUT_OF_DATE / REVIEW_REQUIRED, show the source change, and let an authorized user choose regenerate, update manually, accept unchanged, or supersede.



63. Complete Release-Gate Acceptance Criteria



All earlier acceptance criteria remain in force. The following criteria are added for the Complete Production Hub.



63.1 Production



• Start an approved ShootingDay and see planned scenes/shots.



• Record multiple takes against stable shot IDs.



• Mark circle/director selects and expose them to AC Edit.



• Create continuity records with images and take/scene linkage.



• Create camera and sound reports.



• Generate DPR from actual day events.



• Show schedule variance without AI arithmetic.



63.2 Dailies / media



• Create ingest session and verify checksum.



• Track primary/backup status separately.



• Generate and stream proxy derivative.



• Link source media to scene/shot/take.



• Open dailies review with Sorani/English comments.



• Prevent “verified backup” status when checksum verification has failed or is missing.



63.3 Post and review



• Create edit version and send it to review.



• Frame/timecode comment survives new UI session and retains author/time.



• Approval is tied to immutable version.



• Picture lock emits dependency events.



• Create VFX task/version and approve final.



• Track color/audio/localization versions.



63.4 Sorani localization



• Sorani subtitles render correctly RTL in web preview and export.



• Mixed Kurdish-English names/numbers remain in intended visual order.



• Timed-text QC correctly evaluates timings without corrupting RTL text.



• Kurdish review comments, notifications and production documents export correctly.



63.5 Master/QC/delivery



• Assemble immutable master candidate from approved components.



• Run configured QC profile and persist findings/measurements.



• Failed QC blocks delivery package approval unless authorized override policy explicitly permits it.



• Build delivery package against a versioned delivery profile.



• Readiness view lists exact missing requirements.



• Record delivery submission and accepted/rejected outcome without overwriting prior attempts.



64. Complete Testing Strategy



Testing must include deterministic domain logic, media integrity, RTL/UI visual regression, production concurrency and workflow state transitions.



64.1 Additional automated tests



• Shot/take numbering and duplicate/slate collision rules



• Offline/queued on-set updates reconciliation where implemented



• Checksum and ingest-finalization tests



• Media derivative lineage tests



• Picture-lock → stale dependency tests



• Review approval immutable-version tests



• Subtitle timecode/readability/QC rules



• Audio track/channel declaration validation



• Master component/version integrity



• QC profile version tests



• Delivery package completeness rules



• Permission tests for external reviewer and delivery roles



• Large-upload signed-session expiry/retry behavior



64.2 End-to-end regression project



Maintain one internal bilingual Sorani/English test production that progresses through: script → breakdown → storyboard → budget → schedule → call sheet → production day → takes/continuity → ingest/dailies → AC Edit → review → VFX/color/sound/localization → master → QC → delivery package. The test project must include mixed-direction scene headings, Kurdish subtitles, multiple audio layouts and at least one intentionally failing QC item.



64.3 Load and resilience



• Concurrent on-set users updating production status



• Large media ingest sessions



• Many review comments on a long-form asset



• Long-running QC/package jobs



• Redis/job retry and idempotency



• Object-storage temporary outage behavior



• PostgreSQL fail/retry and transaction boundaries



• Recovery after browser/app reconnect



65. One Master Build — Recommended Engineering Sequence



The entire scope should be approved and architected now, but engineering should proceed in dependency order so teams can work concurrently against stable contracts.



66. Updated Developer Definition of Done



• Implements required backend domain model and frontend workflow.



• Uses canonical project/scene/shot/take/asset/version identifiers.



• Has ckb-IQ + English localization strings and passes RTL visual QA.



• Has server-side permissions and audit logging.



• Has deterministic rules for calculations/status validation; AI is advisory unless explicitly authorized.



• Has version/immutability behavior for approved artifacts.



• Emits/consumes required domain events and stale flags.



• Supports job idempotency/progress for long work.



• Handles Sorani Unicode round-trip through DB/API/export.



• Has unit/API/integration tests and relevant media/large-file tests.



• Has responsive behavior for intended desktop/tablet/mobile use.



• Does not expose secrets or private object-storage assets publicly.



• Has acceptance-test evidence before feature flag is enabled for customers.



67. Immediate Master Developer Handoff Checklist



• Freeze canonical IDs and shared schemas for Project, Scene, Shot, Take, MediaAsset, Version, Approval and DeliveryProfile.



• Implement ckb-IQ/RTL platform infrastructure globally before module-specific UI expansion.



• Add feature-flag/entitlement controls for every new module.



• Finalize domain-event contracts and stale-dependency behavior across the full lifecycle.



• Complete the pre-production modules already specified in Sections 7–12 on the shared architecture.



• Build AC Production dashboard plus Shot/Take and Continuity as the first production wave.



• Implement verified media ingest/checksum/derivative lineage before production-scale dailies.



• Connect Dailies and production selects directly into AC Edit.



• Implement immutable AC Review/version approval framework before VFX/color/sound workflows.



• Add localization/timed-text data model with Sorani RTL tests before subtitle automation.



• Implement Master + QC as separate but connected services.



• Implement delivery profiles/packages/readiness as versioned configuration, not hard-coded one-platform logic.



• Add rights/releases as readiness dependencies and secure document records.



• Expand Production Copilot only after structured services and permissions are reliable.



• Run the complete bilingual regression production from idea through delivery before public launch.



68. Final Product Vision — Art City AI: From Idea to Delivery



The target product is a unified film and media Production Operating System in which AI assists creative and operational decisions while structured production data remains authoritative. Cinema and Studio provide generative creation capabilities; AC Script and the pre-production modules plan the work; AC Production records what actually happened; AC Edit and post modules transform the captured media; Mastering/QC validate the result; Delivery packages and tracks the approved outputs.



Appendix E — Production Status Enums



Appendix F — Example Production Event Payload



Appendix G — Sorani / RTL Production QA Samples



Use these as regression concepts; the QA team should expand them into real fixtures and screenshots.



Appendix H — Delivery Profile Contract (Conceptual)



Appendix I — Non-Scope Boundary



This master specification is intentionally focused on the Art City AI filmmaking and media-production lifecycle. General corporate administration, enterprise HR/payroll, company-wide accounting, unrelated procurement, and unrelated CRM/ERP functions are outside this Production Hub specification. Production-specific budgets, actual-cost references, crew participation, equipment usage, releases and delivery records remain in scope where they directly support a film/media project.

=== TABLE 48 ===



Phase | Deliverables | Why this order



1 — Shared Core | Project model extension, localization/RTL framework, permissions, asset links, versions, audit, AI job framework. | Everything else depends on this.



2 — AC Script | Screenplay editor, imports, AI assist, scene parser, script versions. | Creates canonical scenes/content.



3 — Breakdown Core | Breakdown extraction/editor, character/location registries. | Feeds all production modules.



4 — AC Storyboard | Découpage, shot DB, locks, storyboard generation and exports. | Uses scenes and references.



5 — AC Budget | Rate cards, budget grid, formulas, scenarios, exports. | Uses breakdown; improves once schedule exists.



6 — Schedule Core | Shooting days, constraints, scene assignment, approvals. | Required for reliable call sheets.



7 — AC Call | Call sheet template, weather, distribution, confirmation, revisions. | Depends on approved schedule.



8 — Deep Ecosystem Integration | Cinema/Studio/Edit handoff, production media tagging, advanced cross-module actions. | Turns suite into one operating system.

docs/ART_CITY_VERTICAL_DRAMA_SPEC.md
# Art City AI Vertical Drama IP Factory



Imported from:



- `docs/source/Art_City_AI_Vertical_Drama_IP_Factory_Master_Developer_Specification_v1.0.docx`

- `docs/source/Art_City_AI_Vertical_Drama_IP_Factory_Developer_Sprint_Backlog_v1.0.docx`



Working extracts: `docs/source/*.extract.txt`.



## Product



Public name: **Art City AI Vertical Drama IP Factory**. UI label: **AC Vertical Drama**. Promise: create a series, build an IP, produce episode by episode.



This is a **separate domain** on the shared Art City AI core. It is not a prompt-to-video page and does not duplicate accounts, billing, storage, or AI providers.



## Architecture freeze (ADR)



| Decision | Rule |

|---|---|

| Boundary | `/vertical-drama` under existing Art City auth and project shell |

| Project identity | Shared `project_id` plus domain `vd_project_id` |

| Assets | Shared `assets` / MinIO; VD stores semantic links |

| AI | All inference via Model Gateway / AI Router — never from UI |

| Canon | Structured entities + versioned JSON; AI proposes; humans approve |

| Locks | Approved canon/script/master never silently overwritten |

| Localization | Original language is canonical; translations are linked variants |

| Deletion | Soft-delete + audit |



## Shared vs domain-owned



**Shared:** auth, `projects`, Data Bank/assets, Model Gateway, cost ledger, Hub Script, Cinema/Studio/Edit, ckb-IQ/RTL, QC/delivery primitives.



**Domain-owned:** IP titles, rights/provenance, canon, story bible, seasons/episodes, découpage/shots, VD generation jobs, assemblies, QC runs, delivery packages.



## MVP (Sprints 0–4)



Governed IP → Story Bible → season/episode factory → découpage → router generation → Edit handoff → QC → delivery.



Sprint 5 analytics learning loop is **deferred**.


docs/KURDISH_FIRST_ROADMAP.md
# Kurdish-First Training Roadmap



**Goal:** Art City becomes the first serious Kurdish AI production platform — trained on Kurdish datasets + dialect metadata, with Art City–hosted models as default and external APIs as fallback only.



**Repo:** `zaragoza444/artcity-lab`  

**Status today:** Governance shell is real. GPU training and loadable Kurdish weights are not yet.



---



## North star



```mermaid

flowchart LR

  Archive[LocalKurdishArchive] --> DataLab[DataLabIngest]

  DataLab --> Rights[RightsApproved]

  Rights --> Annotate[AnnotateDialects]

  Annotate --> Manifest[TrainingManifest]

  Manifest --> Train[GPUTrain]

  Train --> Registry[ModelRegistry]

  Registry --> Gateway[ModelGateway]

  Gateway --> Products[SpeechStudioCinema]

```



---



## What already exists



| Layer | Ready? | Notes |

|-------|--------|--------|

| Data Lab ingest / inventory / export | Yes | Multipart → MinIO `datasets/{id}/raw/` |

| Annotations + rights gate → `training_ready` | Yes | Enforced before training jobs |

| Training job API | Partial | Approve is **simulated** (no GPU) |

| Model registry + Kardokh/Kurdiya LoRA labels | Yes | Names/status only — no real weights |

| `AC-KURDISH-ASR-v1` | Shell | Pilot phrase bank, not trained ASR |

| Dialects Sorani / Badini / Kurmanji | Yes | Speech + knowledge pack |

| Cultural knowledge enrichment | Yes | Prompt pack, not embeddings |

| Studio / Cinema / Edit products | Yes | Still often soft-fail to local/`ext` providers |



---



## Phase 0 — Data foundation (1–2 weeks)



**Outcome:** One rights-cleared Kurdish speech corpus + one character image corpus in production Data Lab.



1. Unpack local archive on disk (group by dialect + media type).

2. Ingest via **Data Lab** (`/data-lab`):

   - Speech: wav/mp3 + optional transcripts → dataset `KD-SPEECH-KU-v1` (or new `KD-SPEECH-KU-v2`)

   - Images: Kardokh / Kurdiya / brand stills → character datasets

3. Attach **Rights** with `ai_training=true`, `fine_tuning=true`, approved legal status.

4. Promote datasets to `training_ready`.

5. Annotate: dialect label, speaker, consent, quality; approve annotations.

6. Export training manifest (JSONL) and store in MinIO exports.



**Metadata required on every file**



- `language` (ku) · `dialect` (sorani | badini | kurmanji)  

- `media_type` · checksum · rights_status  

- For speech: speaker_id, duration, transcript if available  

- For image: character_key, scene tags, cultural notes  



**Exit criteria:** Manifest lists real files (not empty `record_count=0`); rights gate passes; export downloadable.



---



## Phase 1 — First owned Kurdish ASR (3–6 weeks)



**Outcome:** Production Speech uses Art City–hosted ASR weights for all three dialects.



1. Replace always-on `PilotAsrEngine` with a real engine slot (Whisper-class fine-tune or equivalent).

2. Extend training approve path to emit **`asr` / speech** models (not hardcoded `lora`/`image`).

3. Add GPU worker (or managed train job) that:

   - pulls Data Lab export / MinIO audio

   - trains / fine-tunes per dialect or multi-dialect

   - writes checkpoint under `models/AC-KURDISH-ASR-vN/`

   - records WER on held-out set

4. Register checkpoint checksum; promote `AC-KURDISH-ASR-vN` → **production**.

5. Wire `resolve_asr_engine()` to load production weights.

6. Live suite: Sorani / Badini / Kurmanji ASR must return real transcripts (not pilot banks).



**Exit criteria:** Speech UI + Cinema VO ASR use hosted model; eval WER documented per dialect; badge `ART CITY-HOSTED` / `FINE-TUNED`.



---



## Phase 2 — Kardokh / Kurdiya image LoRA (4–8 weeks)



**Outcome:** Studio image (and later video) routes apply real adapters — not media-factory placeholders alone.



1. Build image inventories in Data Lab (character sheets, stills, approved generations).

2. Real LoRA train from export (Flux/SD-class base — choose one and stick to it).

3. Store `.safetensors` + checksum in registry (`AC-KARDOKH-IMAGE-v2`, `AC-KURDIYA-IMAGE-v2`).

4. Change gateway/providers to **load adapters** when route resolves to those models.

5. Cultural pack terms stay as prompt enrichment **plus** adapter identity.

6. Eval: blind review + cultural accuracy checklist before production promote.



**Exit criteria:** Generating with `character_key=kardokh|kurdiya` uses hosted LoRA; manifests show `ART CITY FINE-TUNED`.



---



## Phase 3 — Platform honesty + scale (ongoing)



1. Status badges everywhere: `PROXY` / `EXTERNAL` / `ART CITY-HOSTED` / `FINE-TUNED` / `PILOT`.

2. Training + Models UI: create job, approve, promote (not list-only).

3. Voice LoRAs and video adapters after image path is proven.

4. Optional larger Kurdish LM later (needs much more text data + budget).

5. Keep OpenAI/fal as **capacity overflow only**; Kurdish default stays Art City.



---



## Recommended order of work (next concrete actions)



| Priority | Action | Owner surface |

|----------|--------|----------------|

| P0 | Ingest your local Kurdish archive into Data Lab with dialect metadata | `/data-lab` |

| P0 | Rights + `training_ready` on speech + image datasets | `/rights`, dataset status |

| P1 | Zip/bulk ingest if archives are large | Backend Data Lab enhancement |

| P1 | Real ASR engine + GPU train job from speech export | `asr_engine.py`, `registries.py`, worker |

| P2 | Load ASR weights in Speech production path | `speech.py` |

| P2 | Real image LoRA train + load at inference | gateway/providers |

| P3 | Training/Models admin UI + eval dashboards | frontend |



---



## Success definition (first public claim)



Art City can honestly say it is a **Kurdish AI platform** when:



1. Kurdish speech is transcribed by **Art City–hosted** ASR trained on **your** rights-cleared data.  

2. At least one Kurdish character image path uses a **fine-tuned Art City adapter**.  

3. Dialects and cultural metadata are first-class in Data Lab + Knowledge.  

4. External APIs are labeled fallback — not the default “brain.”



Until then, the correct status is: **Kurdish-first product platform with pilot ASR and a training governance shell** — which is the right foundation to finish.


docs/source/Art_City_AI_Vertical_Drama_IP_Factory_Developer_Sprint_Backlog_v1.0.extract.txt
ART CITY AI

VERTICAL DRAMA IP FACTORY

Developer Sprint Backlog & Implementation Handoff

Companion to Master Developer Specification v1.0

Execution Pack v1.0  |  22 August 2026

Development directive

Separate product domain. Shared Art City AI core. Build the IP system before scaling generation.

1. Purpose and Implementation Directive

This document converts the Art City AI Vertical Drama IP Factory master specification into an execution-ready engineering backlog. It is designed for direct use by the technical lead, backend, frontend, AI/ML, DevOps and QA teams. The goal is to remove interpretation from the first build cycle: ticket boundaries, dependencies, coding sequence, acceptance gates and release criteria are defined here.

Do not build Vertical Drama as a generic prompt-to-video page.

Do not fork the Art City AI platform or duplicate accounts, billing, storage, project ownership or provider integrations.

Build a dedicated Vertical Drama domain with its own routes, services, tables and UI, linked to the canonical Art City AI project and asset systems.

Treat Story Bible, Canon, Character DNA, Episode State and Provenance as first-class data, not text blobs.

AI generation must remain provider-agnostic through the shared AI Router.

Sorani Kurdish (ckb-IQ), English and Arabic must be supported from the beginning; RTL is not a post-launch patch.

2. Architecture Freeze Before Coding

The following decisions are frozen for the first implementation unless Art City product leadership explicitly changes them. Developers should not silently replace them with convenient alternatives.

3. Delivery Team and Ticket Ownership

One engineer may hold multiple codes on a small team. The codes identify responsibility, not headcount.

4. Recommended Build Sequence and Release Train

4.1 Critical path

Shared project linkage → Vertical Drama domain schema → IP/Canon → Story Bible → Season/Episode versions → Scene/Shot model → AI jobs/assets → Assembly/QC → Delivery.

Do not start batch video generation before Character DNA, shot identity, versioning, provenance and cost attribution are functional.

Do not introduce analytics-driven rewriting until lock/version semantics are stable.

5. Sprint 0 — Foundation, Domain Boundary and Contracts

Sprint 0 exists to prevent the common failure mode where UI and model calls are built before the data model is stable. The output is a compilable, deployable skeleton with agreed contracts and no duplicated platform infrastructure.

6. Sprint 1 — IP Vault, Canon and Governed Project Shell

7. Sprint 2 — Story Bible, Season Architecture and Episode Factory

8. Sprint 3 — Découpage, Character Consistency and AI Production Pipeline

9. Sprint 4 — Assembly, Localization, QC and Delivery Backlog

Sprint 4 is the first release-completion sprint. It may be scheduled immediately after Sprint 3, but the following tickets should be created now so Sprint 3 interfaces do not paint the system into a corner.

10. Required API Contract Set

The exact framework may remain FastAPI/Next.js as in the wider platform, but these resource contracts should exist before UI logic depends on local component state.

10.1 Write request requirements

Authenticated tenant/project context.

Permission check on server.

request_id/correlation_id.

Expected version or If-Match/optimistic-lock value for mutable resources.

Idempotency-Key on job-generating or expensive requests.

Audit entry for approvals, locks, rights and destructive lifecycle changes.

11. Database Migration Order

Every migration must include indexes for tenant/project scope and foreign keys used by episode/shot retrieval. Use database constraints for invariants that must never be violated, not only service-layer checks.

12. Recommended Code Structure

backend/

  app/vertical_drama/

    api/

    domain/

      ip/

      canon/

      story_bible/

      season/

      episode/

      screenplay/

      production/

      localization/

      qc/

      delivery/

    services/

    repositories/

    schemas/

    events/

    workflows/

    tests/



frontend/

  app/vertical-drama/

    new/

    [projectId]/

      overview/

      ip-vault/

      story-bible/

      characters/

      season/

      episodes/

      production/

      review/

      delivery/

  components/vertical-drama/

  lib/vertical-drama/



shared/

  ai-router/

  assets/

  auth-rbac/

  billing-credits/

  projects/

  audit/

  observability/

Rule: shared services may be imported through stable contracts. Vertical Drama domain code must not reach into another product module’s private tables or internal implementation.

13. Required Domain Events and Dependency Rules

14. AI Workflow Registry — Initial Keys

Model/provider mappings must be managed in the shared registry/admin layer. Domain records should store the resolved provider/model used for a run, but business logic must request capabilities/workflows rather than vendor names.

15. Frontend Build Order

16. Kurdish Sorani / RTL Release Criteria

Use Unicode UTF-8 end-to-end; never transliterate Sorani to store or process it internally.

ckb-IQ content direction is RTL, but IDs, timecodes, file names, URLs and technical fields may remain LTR inside isolated UI containers.

All multi-language content fields must store language code and content separately. Do not combine translations into one text column.

Test punctuation, Arabic-Indic/Latin digits, quotation marks, parentheses, colon/timecode display and mixed English model names inside RTL text.

Exported subtitles and metadata must preserve correct line order and encoding.

AI prompts may use internal English instructions, but the requested content language and cultural context must be explicit and the output schema language-tagged.

Golden tests must include Sorani character names, dialogue, long screenplay paragraphs and right-aligned form fields.

17. Automated Test Matrix

18. Definition of Done for Every Ticket

Code merged after peer review and linked to ticket ID.

API/schema change documented and contract tests updated.

RBAC and tenant/project isolation considered for every server endpoint.

Loading, empty, error, permission-denied and retry states implemented where relevant.

Logs include request/job correlation identifiers; no secrets or raw sensitive tokens logged.

User-facing text supports localization; no English-only hard-coded layout assumption.

Unit/integration tests cover happy path plus at least one important failure path.

No provider-specific AI call is added outside the shared AI Router/provider adapter layer.

AI-derived records include provenance and cost/usage metadata when applicable.

Database migration includes rollback or documented irreversible rationale.

QA evidence attached and acceptance gate explicitly marked pass/fail.

19. MVP Release Gate

Do not call the module production-ready simply because it can generate clips. The MVP is ready when one governed IP can travel through the complete core lifecycle with traceability and human approval.

20. Technical Risks Developers Must Escalate

21. Technical Lead — First Repository Actions

☐ Create one parent epic: AC AI — Vertical Drama IP Factory MVP.

☐ Import Sprint 0 tickets first and freeze ADR/API/ID conventions before feature coding.

☐ Create feature flag and staging-only product card.

☐ Create migration branch and contract-schema package.

☐ Create Vertical Drama backend/frontend module skeletons with CODEOWNERS.

☐ Wire shared auth, project ownership, RBAC, audit, asset store and AI Router — do not clone them.

☐ Create Golden Project A fixture in Sorani before Story/AI features expand.

☐ Require every model workflow to emit validated structured JSON before persistence.

☐ Require every expensive job to show estimated cost/guardrail before batch execution.

☐ Hold an architecture review at the end of Sprint 0 and a release-gate review at the end of every subsequent sprint.

22. Final Engineering Directive

The first success metric is not “we generated a vertical video.” It is “we created a governed entertainment IP whose story, canon, characters, episodes and generated production assets remain consistent, versioned, auditable and reusable.” Once that foundation works, Art City AI can change or add generation models without rebuilding the product.



--- TABLE 1 ---

Decision | Frozen rule

Product boundary | /vertical-drama is a dedicated product area under the existing Art City AI account and project shell.

Project identity | Every Vertical Drama title references the shared project_id; Vertical Drama also owns a vd_project_id/domain aggregate ID.

Asset identity | Generated/reference assets use the shared asset store and immutable asset IDs; Vertical Drama stores semantic links to those assets.

AI providers | No provider-specific calls from UI or domain services. All inference goes through the AI Router/model registry.

Canonical narrative data | Structured entities and versioned JSON are authoritative. Generated prose is a derivative representation.

Canon changes | Approved canon changes emit domain events and mark dependent material stale; they do not silently rewrite approved episodes.

Generation | All expensive generation is asynchronous, idempotent, retryable and cost-attributed.

IP/provenance | Human authorship, source/reference origin, model/provider, prompts, seeds/parameters and output IDs are logged.

Localization | Original-language content remains canonical; translated/adapted versions are linked variants.

Deletion | Soft delete + audit trail for project-domain entities; hard deletion only through privileged data-retention workflow.



--- TABLE 2 ---

Code | Role | Primary responsibility

TL | Technical Lead / Architect | Architecture freeze, review, merge gates, data-contract ownership

BE | Backend Engineer | Domain services, REST APIs, job orchestration, permissions, audit

FE | Frontend Engineer | Product shell, editors, grids, review UX, RTL, state handling

AI | AI / Workflow Engineer | Structured generation, prompt contracts, model routing, evaluation

DB | Backend/DB owner | Migrations, indexes, constraints, versioning, integrity

OPS | DevOps / Platform | Queues, workers, object storage, secrets, observability, deployment

QA | QA / Automation | API/UI tests, golden projects, regression and release evidence

PD | Product/Creative owner | Acceptance of workflows, story logic, quality and terminology



--- TABLE 3 ---

Stage | Suggested cadence | Primary outcome | Exit gate

Sprint 0 — Foundation & Contracts | 1 week | Freeze schemas/API contracts; establish module boundary, migrations, feature flag, queue conventions, observability and test harness. | No story generation until schema/API review passes.

Sprint 1 — IP Vault, Canon & Project Shell | 2 weeks | Create IP/title registry, rights/provenance, characters, canon facts, visual references and Vertical Drama project UX. | A user can create a governed IP project and persist approved canon.

Sprint 2 — Story, Season & Episode Factory | 2 weeks | Concept, Story Bible, season architecture, episode grid, screenplay, hook/pacing/cliffhanger, approval/versioning. | A project can produce and approve a complete structured text season without generating video.

Sprint 3 — Découpage, AI Generation & Asset Pipeline | 3 weeks | Scenes/shots, character reference binding, AI Router workflows, job queue, image/video/voice generation, cost/provenance. | An approved episode can be converted into generated, traceable shot assets.

Sprint 4 — Assembly, QC, Localization & Delivery | 2 weeks | Timeline handoff, subtitles/dubbing, QC, mastering, export packages, delivery readiness. | One mastered 9:16 episode and localized variant passes automated and human QC.

Sprint 5 — Analytics, Optimization & Scale | 2 weeks | Performance ingestion, episode analytics, learning loop, batch controls, admin/provider operations. | Data can improve editorial recommendations without auto-altering locked canon.



--- TABLE 4 ---

ID | P | Owner | Ticket / Deliverable | Dependencies | Acceptance gate

VDF-ARC-001 | P0 | TL | Create Vertical Drama bounded-context ADR and code ownership map. Define what remains shared vs domain-owned. | Master spec | ADR merged; folder/service ownership approved; no duplicate auth/billing/storage implementation.

VDF-ARC-002 | P0 | TL/BE | Define aggregate IDs and resource naming: project_id, vd_project_id, ip_title_id, season_id, episode_id, scene_id, shot_id, version_id. | ARC-001 | IDs documented in OpenAPI/schema package; naming used consistently in migrations and events.

VDF-DB-001 | P0 | DB | Create migration namespace and baseline Vertical Drama schema with audit columns, tenant/project ownership and soft-delete pattern. | ARC-002 | Upgrade/downgrade tested on clean DB and current staging snapshot.

VDF-BE-001 | P0 | BE | Create /api/v1/vertical-drama router, service package and health/capability endpoint behind feature flag. | ARC-001 | Authenticated capability endpoint returns enabled entitlements; disabled flag returns controlled 404/403.

VDF-FE-001 | P0 | FE | Add Vertical Drama product card and /vertical-drama route shell inside existing Art City AI navigation. | BE-001 | Uses existing auth/project selector; feature flag respected; responsive desktop/mobile shell.

VDF-BE-002 | P0 | BE | Define canonical error envelope, optimistic-lock field, request_id and idempotency-key convention for write/generation APIs. | ARC-002 | Contract tests cover validation, conflict, permission and duplicate submission.

VDF-OPS-001 | P0 | OPS | Provision Vertical Drama worker queue names, dead-letter handling, per-job correlation IDs and environment settings. | ARC-001 | Test job can enqueue, run, retry, fail to DLQ and expose trace ID.

VDF-OBS-001 | P1 | OPS/BE | Add structured logs and metrics dimensions: tenant, project, workflow, provider, model, job, cost, latency, result. | OPS-001 | Staging dashboard can filter one synthetic job end-to-end.

VDF-QA-001 | P0 | QA | Create API contract-test harness and one empty golden Vertical Drama project fixture. | DB-001, BE-001 | CI spins DB, applies migrations, creates project, runs contract smoke tests.

VDF-SEC-001 | P0 | BE/TL | Map existing RBAC/entitlements to Vertical Drama actions; define creator, editor, approver, admin and viewer scopes. | ARC-001 | Permission matrix encoded and unit-tested; no endpoint relies only on frontend hiding.

VDF-AI-001 | P0 | AI/TL | Define StructuredAIResponse contract (schema_version, content, warnings, provenance, token/cost usage, model metadata). | ARC-002 | JSON Schema validated in CI; one mock provider response passes and one malformed response fails.

VDF-AI-002 | P1 | AI/BE | Register Vertical Drama workflow keys in shared AI Router without hard-wiring vendors. | AI-001 | Mock route resolves workflow → capability → model/provider with fallback metadata.



--- TABLE 5 ---

Gate | Evidence required | Pass condition

G0.1 Architecture | ADR, folder tree, API namespace, ID dictionary | Technical lead and backend/frontend owners sign off.

G0.2 Data | Baseline migration + rollback evidence | Clean install and upgrade both pass.

G0.3 Platform | Route shell + auth + entitlement + queue smoke test | One authenticated project opens and one mock job completes.

G0.4 Contract | OpenAPI + JSON schemas + contract tests | CI blocks incompatible contract changes.



--- TABLE 6 ---

Risk | Why it matters | Mandatory response

RISK-01 — Text blobs instead of domain data | Fast initially, disastrous for canon checks, localization, versioning and analytics. | Reject designs that store Story Bible/episode/character state as a single unstructured document.

RISK-02 — Provider lock-in | Direct fal.ai or other provider calls inside product code will make migration/cost routing difficult. | All inference through AI Router and workflow keys.

RISK-03 — Weak identity consistency | Video generation before reference-locking leads to changing faces, wardrobe and world continuity. | Block production when required Character DNA/reference bindings are missing.

RISK-04 — Silent AI rewrites | Regeneration can destroy approved creative work. | Immutable versions + approval locks + explicit new draft.

RISK-05 — Cost explosion | Batch video generation can create unexpected spend. | Estimate/guardrail/budget checks before enqueue; cost ledger after each attempt.

RISK-06 — RTL added late | Core forms/grids/editors become costly to repair. | Sorani golden project from Sprint 1 onward.

RISK-07 — Provenance gaps | Cannot prove origin, model use, or human contribution later. | Persist provenance at creation time, not as a future reporting feature.

RISK-08 — Cross-product coupling | Direct access to Cinema/Edit private tables creates brittle dependencies. | Use shared services or explicit contracts/events.

Appendix A–H. Schemas, APIs, States and Example Contracts

1. Executive Directive and Product Decision

Art City AI Vertical Drama IP Factory is a specialized production operating environment for developing, producing, localizing, mastering and commercializing short-form episodic vertical drama IP. It must not be implemented as a single “generate video” page. The product is a persistent story-and-production system in which characters, canon, episodes, shots, assets, rights, versions, approvals, costs and performance data remain connected over time.

The product must create persistent IP, not disposable generations.

AI proposes and accelerates; human users approve canon, rights, episode lock and final masters.

Every expensive generation must be job-tracked, costed, versioned and associated with a Project/Series/Episode/Shot.

Character, voice, wardrobe, location and style consistency are core product functions, not optional prompt tips.

The system must support AI-native, hybrid live-action and conventional-production-assisted vertical drama.

Kurdish Sorani is a first-class writing, UI, subtitle, dubbing and metadata language.

Provider/model names must be abstracted behind Art City model/workflow labels and the Art City AI Router.

1.1 Recommended product position

Public/product name: Art City AI Vertical Drama IP Factory. Short UI label: AC Vertical Drama. Product promise: “Create a series. Build an IP. Produce episode by episode.” The word “IP” should remain visible because the differentiation is not merely fast vertical video generation; it is persistent franchise development and controlled production.

1.2 The key architecture answer

2. Separation Strategy: Separate Domain, Shared Core

The product should be “separate where specialization creates value, shared where duplication creates risk.” Vertical drama requires season/episode/canon/continuity logic that does not belong inside the generic Studio interface. At the same time, duplicating user accounts, projects, assets, AI credentials, billing and QC would create data fragmentation and unnecessary engineering cost.

2.1 Shared platform services

Authentication, organizations/workspaces, users, teams and invitations.

Canonical Project service and project_id.

Asset Library / Data Bank, object storage, previews, versions and lineage.

Art City AI Router, Provider Registry, Model Registry and job/cost ledger.

Subscriptions, credits, plan entitlements, usage limits and Art City approval/permission gates.

Localization framework and ckb-IQ/RTL infrastructure.

Notification center, audit timeline, comments/review and approval primitives.

Art City Studio image/video/voice/music asset generation.

Art City Cinema cinematic sequence/campaign generation where appropriate.

Art City Edit assembly, timeline, repurposing, captioning and finishing.

Production Hub Script/Storyboard/Budget/Call Sheet objects when a drama uses conventional/hybrid production.

QC, Mastering, Delivery and global search.

2.2 Vertical-drama-owned domain services

IP/Franchise registry and story canon.

Series, season, episode and serial-narrative architecture.

Episode beat templates, hooks, cliffhangers and continuity checks.

Character identity locks and long-running appearance/wardrobe variants.

World/location continuity and reusable production “locks.”

Episode factory/orchestration state machine.

Vertical-drama-specific shot planning and safe-zone composition metadata.

Episode-to-episode localization/remake lineage.

Performance analytics mapped back to episode beats, scenes and versions.

Rights/provenance contributions associated with a persistent IP title.

2.3 Recommended code boundary

frontend/app/[locale]/vertical-drama/

frontend/app/[locale]/projects/[projectId]/vertical-drama/

3. Product Definition and Target Users

The product serves creators and production companies that need serial short-form drama output at a cadence and volume that conventional one-off generation tools do not manage well. It should support professional production control without forcing every user into film-industry complexity on day one.

3.1 Supported content structures

Anthology series with separate episode stories.

Continuous serialized drama with season-long arc.

Limited series.

Multi-season franchise.

AI-native fiction.

Animation / stylized drama.

Hybrid AI + live action.

User-owned adaptation/remake, only after rights declaration and rights record.

Localized versions of an existing Art City-managed IP.

4. Scope, Modes and Non-Goals

4.1 Four production modes

4.2 Product defaults, not hard-coded limits

4.3 Explicit non-goals for MVP

Building a full consumer streaming/payment app for viewers inside this module.

Replacing Art City Edit with a complete professional nonlinear editor.

Automatic legal determination of copyright ownership or infringement.

Automatic public publishing to every platform without authorized APIs and user permission.

Fully autonomous showrunning with no human canon/rights/final-master approval.

Hard-wiring the product to one image/video/voice provider.

Guaranteeing “viral” performance from AI scoring.

  ↓

EPISODE SCRIPT → SCENES → DÉCOUPAGE / SHOTS

  ↓

  ↓

IMAGE / VIDEO / VOICE / MUSIC / SFX GENERATION

  ↓

ASSEMBLY → EDIT → SUBTITLES / DUB → REVIEW → LOCK

  ↓

VERTICAL MASTER → QC → DELIVERY PACKAGE

  ↓

PUBLISH / HANDOFF → ANALYTICS IMPORT

  ↓

PERFORMANCE INSIGHTS → FUTURE EPISODE RECOMMENDATIONS



At every approval gate: version + user + timestamp + lineage + cost + rights state.

5.1 Recommended state machine

6. Domain Architecture and Canonical IDs

Project is the platform container; IP is the franchise/story ownership container; Series/Season/Episode are the serial narrative containers. Do not use Project and Series interchangeably. One Project may contain one principal IP title in MVP; the data model should still permit multiple related series/spin-offs under one IP later.

8. IP Vault and Rights / Provenance Registry

The IP Vault is the strategic differentiator. It should provide production governance, not pretend to be a government copyright registry. It records what Art City/customer claims or owns, what source material was used, which human creators contributed, what AI systems assisted, and which licenses/territories/terms apply. Legal ownership questions still require appropriate human/legal review.

8.1 IP Title fields

IPTitle {

  id, workspace_id, project_id,

  title_display, title_alt[], slug,

  logline, synopsis,

  genre[], tone[], audience_tags[],

  original_language, target_territories[],

  creator_users[], contributor_ids[],

  owner_entity, ownership_basis,

  source_material_type, source_material_reference,

  rights_status, rights_notes,

  trademark_status_optional,

  canonical_story_bible_version_id,

  canonical_visual_bible_version_id,

  status, created_at, updated_at

}

8.2 Rights record

8.3 Human contribution ledger

For each major creative object, log material human contributions independently of AI generation logs. This supports internal provenance, future rights evidence and transparent collaboration. Do not collapse every contribution into “AI generated.”

Original concept authored/edited by.

Story bible authored/edited/approved by.

Character design direction and selected references.

Episode script human revisions and lock approver.

Shot selection and visual direction decisions.

Edit decisions, dialogue performance direction and final approval.

Translations, adaptations and cultural edits.

Music/composer/performer contributions and licenses.

9.1 Entry modes

Start from one-sentence idea.

Start from genre + audience + territory.

Adapt an existing Art City IP with authorization.

Create a spin-off from an existing IP/character.

Create a localized/remake version from a cleared source series.
