10. Story Bible and Canon Engine

The Story Bible is the canonical narrative source of truth. The model may suggest changes, but downstream episode generation must always read an approved bible version unless the user deliberately chooses an experimental branch.

10.1 Canon fact model

CanonFact {

  id, ip_id, category,

  subject_type, subject_id,

  fact_text,

  valid_from_episode,

  valid_to_episode_optional,

  secrecy_level,

  source_bible_version_id,

  status: PROPOSED | CANON | RETCONNED,

  approved_by, approved_at

}

10.2 Canon conflict checker

Run before episode script approval and before generating expensive production assets.

Check character age/relationship/status, injuries, possessions, location rules, timeline, revealed secrets and prior episode outcomes.

Return specific conflicting facts and source episode/bible references.

Do not auto-correct locked scripts; create proposed fixes and require selection.

Retcons must create explicit canonical change records rather than silently overwriting history.

11. Season Architecture Engine

A season should be planned as structured narrative data before mass episode generation. The system may permit “fast mode,” but even fast mode should create an inspectable episode grid and dependency graph.

11.1 Season arc object

Season {

  id, series_id, season_number, title,

  target_episode_count, target_episode_seconds,

  opening_state, midpoint_state, climax_state, ending_state,

  primary_arc, secondary_arcs[],

  character_arc_ids[],

  mystery/payoff_plan[],

  episode_grid_version_id,

  status, approved_by, approved_at

}

11.2 Episode grid columns

11.3 Batch generation safety

Do not generate 80 final scripts in one opaque call. Generate structured episode outlines in batches, validate continuity, allow user approval, then expand selected/approved outlines into scripts. This lowers hallucinated canon drift and prevents expensive downstream rework.

12. Episode Factory and Screenplay Engine

12.1 Episode creation pipeline

EPISODE GRID ROW

 → EPISODE OBJECT

 → BEAT SHEET

 → SCENE OUTLINE

 → DIALOGUE / ACTION DRAFT

 → TIMING ESTIMATE

 → CONTINUITY CHECK

 → HOOK/CLIFFHANGER CHECK

 → HUMAN REVIEW

 → SCRIPT LOCK

 → SHOT / PRODUCTION PIPELINE

12.2 Episode object

Episode {

  id, season_id, episode_number,

  title, logline, synopsis,

  target_runtime_seconds,

  hook_beat_id, cliffhanger_beat_id,

  beat_ids[], scene_ids[],

  script_version_id,

  canon_snapshot_version_id,

  production_mode,

  language,

  status,

  locked_at, locked_by,

  master_asset_id,

  delivery_status

}

12.3 Screenplay integration

Reuse AC Script semantics and editor infrastructure where possible. Vertical Drama owns the serial context and episode pipeline; AC Script remains the professional structured writing component. Episode scripts should map into the same Scene/Character/Location objects used by the Production Hub to preserve interoperability.

Scene heading, action, character, dialogue, parenthetical, transition, shot and notes remain structured types.

Per-episode screenplay templates can optimize for short runtime without inventing a second text model.

Kurdish/English/Arabic mixed-direction text must use the same ckb-IQ/RTL infrastructure as AC Script.

Script lock creates immutable version metadata; later changes create a new version and mark dependent shots/assets stale.

13. Hook, Pacing and Cliffhanger Engine

This engine is an editorial assistant, not a “virality guarantee.” It analyzes whether the episode delivers its configured narrative template and offers alternatives. Users can disable or customize it by genre and broadcaster/platform policy.

13.1 Beat roles

13.2 Editorial checks

Runtime allocation per beat.

Time to first conflict/question.

Exposition density.

Repeated information across adjacent episodes.

Continuity required to understand opening.

Cliffhanger repetition pattern (avoid identical trick every episode).

Character agency versus passive exposition.

Dialogue length relative to target runtime.

Potential content/rating conflicts.

13.3 Output rule

Return findings as structured notes with severity, evidence/beat reference and suggested alternatives. Never silently rewrite a locked episode.

14. Scene, Découpage and Shot Engine

Reuse the AC Storyboard/découpage infrastructure but add vertical-drama composition metadata and identity/style-lock references. Every generated shot must be tied to an approved scene and shot plan or explicitly marked as exploratory.

Shot {

  id, episode_id, scene_id, shot_number,

  purpose, description,

  framing, angle, movement,

  duration_estimate_seconds,

  aspect_ratio: "9:16",

  safe_zone_profile_id,

  subject_character_variant_ids[],

  location_variant_id,

  wardrobe_variant_ids[], prop_ids[],

  style_lock_id,

  continuity_requirements[],

  dialogue_cue_ids[],

  generation_strategy,

  prompt_spec_id,

  status

}

14.1 Vertical composition requirements

Subject placement optimized for 9:16 rather than cropping 16:9 masters.

Configurable text/UI safe zones for delivery platforms; profiles are admin-managed and versioned.

Close/medium framing templates for dialogue, with deliberate wide shots rather than accidental empty space.

Face/eye-line continuity metadata between reverse angles.

Motion paths and camera movements evaluated for vertical frame boundaries.

Generate alternate 16:9/1:1 only as derivatives when needed; 9:16 is the creative master for Vertical Drama projects.

15. Character / Face Consistency System

Character consistency is a release-critical capability. Prompt-only character names are not sufficient. The platform must maintain canonical identity references, approved appearance variants and provider-specific implementation adapters.

15.1 Character DNA

15.2 Appearance variants

A character may change over story time. Create explicit variants such as “Episode 01 baseline,” “after injury,” “wedding wardrobe,” “10 years earlier,” rather than editing the canonical character invisibly. Each shot references one or more CharacterAppearanceVariant IDs.

15.3 Real-person likeness rule

If a character is based on a real actor/person or uses uploaded likeness/voice material, require a rights/consent declaration and link the relevant release/license record. The system should support a policy flag that prevents generation when required rights status is not cleared.

16. World, Location, Wardrobe and Prop Continuity

16.1 Continuity ledger

ContinuityEvent {

  id, episode_id, scene_id, shot_id_optional,

  entity_type, entity_id,

  event_type: ENTER | EXIT | CHANGE | DAMAGE | REVEAL | TRANSFER | OTHER,

  before_state, after_state,

  canon_effect,

  source_version_id,

  approved_by

}

17. Visual Style Lock and Reference System

A Style Lock is an Art City abstraction that records creative intent separately from provider-specific prompt syntax. The same style should be reproducible across multiple providers/workflows without storing only a single raw prompt.

StyleLock {

  id, ip_id, name,

  medium, realism_level,

  palette_description,

  lighting_rules,

  lens/composition_language,

  texture/grain_rules,

  camera_motion_rules,

  production_design_rules,

  negative_rules[],

  reference_asset_ids[],

  provider_adapters: {...},

  version, status, approved_by

}

17.1 Visual Bible approval

Generate exploratory look frames before episode production.

Select and lock approved character/world/style references.

Do not allow bulk episode generation to start if mandatory identity/style locks are missing.

Any change to a locked Style Lock produces a new version and marks affected pending shots for review.

18. AI Casting, Voice and Dialogue Production

Voice is part of character identity. Separate fictional Character, performer/cast record and generated VoiceProfile. This supports real actors, synthetic voices, dubbing and recasting without destroying character canon.

18.1 Voice rules

Never expose provider voice IDs as the only canonical identifier.

Require explicit rights/consent when cloning or imitating a real person’s voice.

Keep original dialogue and each translated/dubbed version separately.

Support pronunciation dictionaries for Kurdish names, locations and culturally specific terms.

Allow user to select one approved voice take per cue and preserve alternates.

19. Video Generation and Shot Production

19.1 Generation strategies

19.2 Normalized generation request

GenerationRequest {

  workspace_id, project_id, ip_id, episode_id, scene_id, shot_id,

  task: "video.generate",

  artcity_workflow_key,

  prompt_spec_id,

  reference_asset_ids[],

  character_variant_ids[],

  location_variant_id,

  style_lock_id,

  duration_seconds,

  aspect_ratio,

  fps_target,

  quality_tier,

  max_cost_usd_optional,

  user_id,

  idempotency_key

}

19.3 Shot generation UX

Generate 1–4 candidates depending on plan/credits.

Show estimated cost before execution when practical.

Queue state: QUEUED / RUNNING / SUCCEEDED / FAILED / CANCELLED.

Candidate comparison with prompt/reference/model/cost metadata.

Select → approve → attach as shot asset.

Rejected candidates remain in lineage/audit per retention policy but are not treated as canon.

Regenerate must create a new Generation record; never overwrite prior result.

20. Audio, Music and Sound Design

Audio should be generated/managed as separate tracks so localization and later mastering are possible. A flattened video with permanently baked dialogue/music is acceptable only as a user-selected low-control mode.

20.1 Music safety and rights

Generated or licensed music must retain source/provider/license terms in the rights/provenance ledger. The platform must not label music “copyright free” merely because an AI model generated it. Delivery readiness should show missing/unclear music rights as a blocker or warning according to policy.

21. Assembly, Edit and Versioning

Vertical Drama should orchestrate episode assembly but should reuse Art City Edit for timeline operations and finishing. The Vertical Drama module owns episode/shot order, selected takes and narrative status; Edit owns timeline-level manipulation, captions, color/finishing and export operations.

21.1 Episode timeline handoff

Vertical Drama Episode

  selected ShotAssets + DialogueTakes + Music/SFX cues

        ↓

Create/Edit Timeline in Art City Edit

        ↓

rough_cut_v1 → review notes → cut_v2 → picture_lock

        ↓

return timeline_id + approved picture asset/version to Episode

21.2 Version rules

Every episode cut has an immutable version identifier.

Review comments bind to version + timecode/frame.

Picture lock is a controlled approval state, not a filename convention.

A post-lock change creates a new cut version and invalidates downstream QC/master status until re-approved.

Never delete approved masters automatically when a new version is created.

22. Localization, Dubbing and Cultural Adaptation

Localization is more than translation. The system must support direct translation, dubbed version, subtitle version and licensed cultural remake as distinct derivative types with lineage back to the source episode/IP.

22.1 Kurdish Sorani requirements

ckb-IQ as explicit locale; not generic “ku”.

Correct RTL subtitles and UI.

Mixed Kurdish/English names and numbers must not visually reorder.

Pronunciation dictionaries for TTS/dubbing.

Human linguistic approval before master delivery.

Preserve original authored Kurdish text; search normalization is separate.

Support parallel original/translation script view.

23. Review, Approval and Canon Locking

23.1 Canon locking rule

24. Vertical Mastering and QC

24.1 Objective technical checks

Aspect ratio and dimensions match delivery profile.

Frame rate/container/codec/profile.

Duration and expected lead/trail.

Black/freeze/corrupt-frame heuristics where supported.

Audio presence, channel configuration, sample rate and loudness/true peak targets.

A/V sync where measurable.

Subtitle cue timing, overlap, reading speed, line limits and RTL render validation.

No missing required stems, textless elements, artwork or metadata.

File checksum and manifest.

24.2 Vertical-drama editorial/continuity warnings

Character identity mismatch relative to approved references.

Wardrobe/prop/location state mismatch.

Dialogue mismatch with locked script.

Unexpected shot orientation/cropping.

Unsafe UI/text area relative to selected platform profile.

Episode numbering/title mismatch.

Missing cliffhanger only when the series template requires one.

Potential duplicated/generated frame or obvious generation artifact heuristics.

Objective checks may block automatically; heuristic AI findings should be warnings requiring human review unless Art City explicitly configures a deterministic rule.

25. Delivery / Publishing Package Builder

Delivery profiles must be configuration-driven because platform requirements change. Do not hard-code TikTok/Instagram/YouTube/dedicated microdrama specifications into business logic. Admin should be able to create/update delivery profiles with version history.

25.1 Delivery readiness

Show a readiness percentage only as a summary. Always display concrete missing/failed requirements. A score must never hide a blocker such as missing master, failed audio layout, missing rights, rejected subtitles or unresolved QC.

26. Analytics and Performance Learning Loop

Analytics turns the factory into a learning system, but it must not rewrite existing canon automatically. Performance data may come from connected platform APIs, CSV import or manual entry depending on authorization and availability.

26.1 Performance analyst output

Identify patterns with confidence/limitations, not causal certainty.

Compare episodes within the same series and comparable cohorts.

Suggest future episode pacing/hook experiments.

Never alter locked episodes automatically.

Keep a record of recommendation → user decision → later outcome for learning.

Do not build manipulative dark-pattern viewer mechanics into the production tool.

27. AI Agents and Orchestration Rules

“Agents” should be implemented as specialized orchestration roles over structured state, not as independent chatbots with uncontrolled memory. Every agent reads approved/current domain objects, writes a proposed structured result, and passes through validation/approval rules.

27.1 Agent constraints

All agent inputs include explicit workspace/project/IP/season/episode context.

All structured outputs validated by JSON Schema/Pydantic.

Prompt templates are versioned and administrator-controlled.

Agents cannot approve their own output unless a product policy explicitly defines a low-risk auto-approval path.

Agents never bypass rights status, locked canon or spending limits.

Use retrieval from Art City’s canonical objects; do not rely on conversational memory for production truth.

28. AI Router and Provider Abstraction

Vertical Drama must consume the shared Art City AI Router defined for the wider platform. Product code calls Art City tasks/workflows; provider adapters translate those requests to fal.ai, private GPU, LLM or CPU implementation. This prevents vendor lock-in and allows cost/quality routing.

AIProvider

  generate_text()

  generate_structured()

  generate_image()

  generate_video()

  edit_image()

  edit_video()

  generate_audio()

  transcribe()

  lip_sync()

  upscale()

  check_status()

  cancel_job()

  estimate_cost()

  health_check()



Vertical Drama calls:

  ai_router.execute(task, workflow_key, normalized_request)

NOT:

  fal_client.some_model(...)

  runpod_endpoint(...)

  provider-specific code in React components

28.1 Workload placement

28.2 Model Registry

Admin must map Art City workflow keys to eligible providers/models, quality tier, VRAM requirement, cost basis, health, fallback and allowed plans. Never expose infrastructure complexity to normal users unless Art City chooses to show an “Advanced model” selector.

29. Job Queue, State Machine and Reliability

Use Redis-backed durable job orchestration/worker system or equivalent.

Every expensive AI operation is asynchronous and resumable.

Browser refresh must not lose job state.

Use idempotency keys to prevent double-generation/double-charge.

Separate normalized ProductJob from ProviderJob so provider retry/fallback does not create duplicate user-visible work.

Support cancellation when provider allows; billing follows actual provider policy.

Store error category, provider error, retry count, fallback decision and final status.

Limit parallel generation by plan/workspace/project to control spend.

Bulk season production is a parent BatchJob containing per-shot/per-cue child jobs.

Do not mark an episode complete merely because all provider jobs returned; require selection/approval/master states.

29.1 Job states

CREATED → VALIDATING → ESTIMATED → QUEUED → DISPATCHED → RUNNING → POSTPROCESSING → SUCCEEDED

                                             ↘ RETRY_WAIT ↗

                                             ↘ FAILED / CANCELLED

30. Data Model and Suggested Database Tables

Use PostgreSQL. The exact ORM is implementation choice, but the relationships and tenant boundaries below should remain. Every domain table must contain or be securely joinable to workspace_id/project_id for authorization and cost attribution.

30.1 Critical database rules

Foreign keys wherever practical; do not rely on arbitrary JSON for core relationships.

JSONB is acceptable for provider-specific settings, flexible metadata and snapshot payloads, but not as a substitute for canonical entities.

Approved versions are immutable; edits create new version rows.

Soft-delete/archive production objects when history must be retained.

All money uses Decimal/numeric, never binary float.

Store timestamps in UTC; render in user/project timezone.

Store locale/language as BCP 47 or controlled language tag fields.

Normalize search indexes without destructively modifying display text.

31. API Surface

Use versioned internal/public API routes. The following is a minimum conceptual surface; naming may be adjusted to existing Art City conventions.

31.1 API requirements

RBAC/tenant authorization server-side on every route.

Idempotency header for generation/charge-producing POST operations.

Structured validation errors with localization keys.

Optimistic locking/version field for concurrent draft edits where appropriate.

Pagination/filter/search conventions shared with Art City core.

No provider API keys or provider request payloads exposed to frontend clients.

Signed/time-limited asset URLs for private media.

32. Domain Events and Dependency Propagation

The platform should respond to approved changes through domain events and stale-dependency flags instead of silently overwriting downstream work.

32.1 Stale dependency UX

Show: “Episode 12 script changed after storyboard approval. Affected: 4 shots, 3 dialogue cues, 1 subtitle draft.” Provide Review Changes and Update Selected actions. Do not regenerate automatically without user decision if it creates cost or replaces approved creative work.

38. Subscription, Entitlements, Credits and Cost Ledger

Vertical Drama must plug into the existing Art City subscription/permission model. Feature access and spending limits should be configurable by plan/workspace without code deployment. External users may require Art City approval before high-cost or rights-sensitive features are enabled, according to platform policy.

38.1 Cost guardrails

Project/season monthly budget cap.

Per-job max cost.

Bulk batch preflight estimate.

Pause batch if actual cost exceeds threshold.

Plan-based quality tier/routing.

Admin ability to disable expensive workflow/provider.

No double charge on retries caused by Art City system failure where policy allows.

Cost shown per successful selected/mastered episode for management analytics.

39. Security, Privacy, Rights and AI Provenance

Workspace/tenant isolation on every database query and asset lookup.

Signed short-lived private asset URLs; no public bucket paths for private scripts/character refs.

Provider API keys/secrets server-side only and encrypted/secret-managed.

Audit sensitive actions: rights clearance, bible lock, script lock, spend override, master approval, delivery, delete/archive.

Configurable prompt/media retention and provider data handling policy.

Do not train Art City/customer models on customer scripts/assets unless explicit policy/contract/consent allows it.

User content rights declaration on upload/adaptation/remake flows.

Likeness/voice consent linkage when real people are used.

AI-generated content lineage: provider/model/workflow version, prompt template version, source/reference asset IDs, generation time, selected/rejected state.

Admin moderation/content-policy layer before dispatch to external providers when required.

Private legal/right documents should have stricter permission scope than general creative assets.

39.1 Provenance record

ProvenanceRecord {

  object_type, object_id,

  origin: HUMAN | AI_ASSISTED | AI_GENERATED | IMPORTED | LICENSED,

  user_id,

  source_asset_ids[],

  source_object_ids[],

  provider, model, workflow_version,

  prompt_template_version,

  generation_id_optional,

  human_revision_summary_optional,

  rights_record_ids[],

}

API latency/error rate by endpoint.

AI job latency/success/failure/cancel rate by workflow/provider/model.

Generation acceptance rate (selected candidates ÷ generated candidates).

Cost per generation, selected shot, mastered episode, minute and season.

Queue depth/wait time and private GPU utilization.

Provider fallback frequency and reason.

Continuity conflict count and resolution rate.

Average revisions per script/shot/episode.

Time from episode planned → script locked → master approved.

QC failures by rule.

Delivery failure/retry by destination profile.

Sorani-specific regression/error metrics where feasible.

Logs must not contain raw confidential scripts, prompts, dialogue, private URLs or access tokens by default. Store identifiers and structured diagnostic metadata; enable privileged content debugging only through explicit controlled mechanisms.

42. Testing Strategy and Golden Test Projects

42.1 Automated tests

Unit tests for state transitions, permissions, canon conflict rules, money/cost calculation, localization and delivery readiness.

Schema validation tests for every structured AI output.

Repository tests enforcing workspace isolation.

Integration tests with mocked AI providers for generation/retry/fallback/idempotency.

Contract tests for provider adapters.

RTL component tests and mixed-direction text fixtures.

Golden screenshot/render tests for vertical frame UI and Sorani subtitles.

Load tests for batch season queues and websocket/polling status updates.

Migration tests for versioned bibles/scripts/canon.

Security tests for signed asset URLs, cross-tenant access and role escalation.

42.2 Minimum golden test projects

43. Acceptance Criteria / Release Gate

AC-VD-001  A user signs in once and creates a Vertical Drama Project using the existing Art City workspace/account.

AC-VD-002  Creating Vertical Drama does not create a duplicate Project, Asset store or billing account.

AC-VD-003  User can create/register an IP record and attach at least one rights/contribution record.

AC-VD-004  User can create and approve a Story Bible version.

AC-VD-005  User can create canonical characters and approved visual references/appearance variants.

AC-VD-006  User can create a season and generate/edit/approve an episode grid.

AC-VD-007  User can create an episode beat sheet, screenplay draft and lock the script.

AC-VD-008  Continuity checker identifies at least configured fact/state conflicts and links evidence.

AC-VD-009  User can generate/edit a shot plan and link vertical composition + style/character references.

AC-VD-010  AI shot generation runs through the Art City AI Router and records provider/model/cost/lineage.

AC-VD-011  User can compare generated candidates and select/approve one without overwriting others.

AC-VD-012  Dialogue cues can generate/attach voice takes with language and rights metadata.

AC-VD-013  User can hand selected episode assets to Art City Edit and receive a timeline/version reference back.

AC-VD-014  Picture lock and master approval are immutable states that create new versions after changes.

AC-VD-015  Sorani ckb-IQ works across story bible, characters, scripts, episode metadata, UI and subtitle/export flow.

AC-VD-016  Mixed RTL/LTR technical values render correctly.

AC-VD-017  Localization variant preserves source lineage and separate approvals.

AC-VD-018  QC distinguishes objective failures from heuristic warnings.

AC-VD-019  Delivery profile lists missing requirements and builds a manifest/checksum package when ready.

AC-VD-020  Rights state can block delivery when policy requires.

AC-VD-021  Every expensive job is idempotent, job-tracked and cost-attributed.

AC-VD-022  Bulk generation survives browser refresh and partial provider failures.

AC-VD-023  Cross-tenant access tests fail correctly.

AC-VD-024  Admin can change workflow/provider routing and pricing configuration without product code deployment.

AC-VD-025  Analytics can import at least CSV/manual performance metrics and map them to episodes.

AC-VD-026  Performance recommendations never modify locked canon automatically.

44. Phased Development Plan

The complete architecture should be agreed now, but code should be released in controlled phases. Avoid attempting every advanced feature in the first deploy; preserve schemas and interfaces so later phases do not require a rewrite.

Appendix B — Structured AI Output Contract

Every AI response that changes production data must use a defined schema. Free-form prose can be displayed as assistant commentary, but it must not be persisted as canonical production state without transformation/validation.

class EpisodeGridItem(BaseModel):

    episode_number: int

    working_title: str

    opening_hook: str

    episode_goal: str

    a_story: str

    b_story: str | None

    revelation: str | None

    character_turn: str | None

    cliffhanger: str | None

    continuity_dependencies: list[str]

    proposed_new_canon: list[str]

    production_complexity: Literal['LOW','MEDIUM','HIGH']

    assumptions: list[str]



class EpisodeGridResult(BaseModel):

    season_id: UUID

    bible_version_id: UUID

    items: list[EpisodeGridItem]

    warnings: list[str]

Appendix C — Minimal FastAPI Generation Contract

@router.post('/shots/{shot_id}/generate')

async def generate_shot(

    shot_id: UUID,

    req: ShotGenerateRequest,

    user=Depends(require_permission('vertical_drama.shot.generate')),

):

    shot = await shot_service.get_authorized(shot_id, user)

    await rights_policy.assert_generation_allowed(shot)

    await budget_policy.assert_within_limit(shot.project_id, req.max_cost_usd)



    normalized = await production_service.build_generation_request(

        shot=shot,

        user=user,

        request=req,

    )

    job = await ai_router.queue(normalized, idempotency_key=req.idempotency_key)

    return JobResponse.model_validate(job)

Appendix F — Prompt Engineering Rules

Prompt templates are server-side and versioned.

Use explicit locale/output_language.

Inject only necessary approved canon/context, not the entire workspace indiscriminately.

Use IDs/reference labels so generated output can map back to canonical objects.

Require structured output schemas for production data.

Separate creative instruction from safety/rights/provider constraints.

Never ask the model to calculate authoritative budget or rights status.

Store prompt_template_version and input-object hashes in job lineage.

Use Sorani examples in ckb-IQ templates and regression-test them.

Do not place provider secrets or private signed URLs into model prompts unless technically required and approved.

Appendix G — Definition of Done for a Mastered Episode

IP and rights policy allow production/delivery.

Story Bible/canon snapshot identified.

Episode script version locked.

All final shots selected/approved.

Dialogue/music/SFX sources and rights/provenance recorded.

Picture lock approved.

Required localization tracks approved.

Master assembled from approved components.

QC passed or authorized documented override exists.

Episode metadata/number/title/language correct.

Manifest/checksum generated.

Master marked immutable with version and approver.

Delivery package created only from approved master.

Appendix H — Final Developer Directive

Recommended internal launch sequence: first make one 10-episode Sorani test IP work end-to-end with story bible, character locks, episode continuity, generated shots, Edit handoff and final vertical masters. After that golden path is stable, scale to 30–80 episode factories and multi-language/remake workflows.

POST | /api/v1/vertical-drama/ip/{ip_id}/characters | Create character.

POST | /api/v1/vertical-drama/characters/{id}/references/generate | Generate character references.

POST | /api/v1/vertical-drama/ip/{ip_id}/style-locks | Create style lock.

POST | /api/v1/vertical-drama/series | Create series.

POST | /api/v1/vertical-drama/seasons | Create season.

POST | /api/v1/vertical-drama/seasons/{id}/episode-grid/generate | Generate episode grid proposal.

POST | /api/v1/vertical-drama/episodes | Create episode.

POST | /api/v1/vertical-drama/episodes/{id}/beats/generate | Generate beat sheet.

POST | /api/v1/vertical-drama/episodes/{id}/script/generate | Generate script draft.

POST | /api/v1/vertical-drama/episodes/{id}/script/{version}/lock | Lock script.

POST | /api/v1/vertical-drama/episodes/{id}/continuity/check | Run canon/continuity check.

POST | /api/v1/vertical-drama/scenes/{id}/decoupage | Generate shot plan.

POST | /api/v1/vertical-drama/shots/{id}/generate | Queue shot generation.

POST | /api/v1/vertical-drama/shots/{id}/select | Select candidate asset.

POST | /api/v1/vertical-drama/dialogue/{cue_id}/generate | Generate voice takes.

POST | /api/v1/vertical-drama/episodes/{id}/assemble | Create/update Art City Edit timeline.

POST | /api/v1/vertical-drama/episodes/{id}/localize | Create localization variant.

POST | /api/v1/vertical-drama/episodes/{id}/qc | Run QC.

POST | /api/v1/vertical-drama/episodes/{id}/master | Build master candidate.

POST | /api/v1/vertical-drama/episodes/{id}/deliveries | Create delivery package.

POST | /api/v1/vertical-drama/episodes/{id}/analytics/import | Import performance data.

GET | /api/v1/vertical-drama/dashboard | Workspace/project dashboard data.



--- TABLE 31 ---

Event | Potential downstream invalidation

STORY_BIBLE_APPROVED | Season arcs/episodes created from older bible become review-required.

CANON_FACT_CHANGED | Future episode scripts, continuity reports.

CHARACTER_VARIANT_CHANGED | Pending storyboards/shots/voice/wardrobe refs.

STYLE_LOCK_CHANGED | Pending/generated shots requiring visual re-review.

SCRIPT_LOCKED_NEW_VERSION | Shot plans, dialogue cues, edit timelines, subtitles.

SHOT_SELECTION_CHANGED | Episode edit/timeline/master/QC.

PICTURE_LOCK_CHANGED | Audio, localization, subtitles, mastering, QC, delivery.

LOCALIZATION_CHANGED | Target-language master/QC/delivery only.

RIGHTS_STATUS_RESTRICTED | Block affected generation/publishing/delivery according to policy.



--- TABLE 32 ---

Mode | UI behavior

Guided | Wizard-like progression; hides advanced production settings.

Professional | Full season grid, versioning, locks, queues and cost controls.

On-set/Hybrid | Touch-friendly episode/scene/shot/continuity controls and dailies handoff.

Review | Minimal player + comments + approve/request changes.

Admin | Provider/workflow/cost/policy settings separated from production UI.



--- TABLE 33 ---

Module | Vertical Drama integration

Projects | Same project_id/workspace_id and global dashboard context.

AC Script / Development | Episode screenplay editor, ScriptVersion, Scene and Character links.

AC Storyboard | Découpage/shot planning and storyboard frames; Vertical Drama adds episode/canon/style context.

AC Budget | Optional per-season/episode hybrid/live-action budgets; AI generation spend remains cost ledger.

AC Call / Schedule | Used for hybrid/live-action vertical productions.

Studio | Generate/modify character sheets, props, locations, posters, individual video/audio/image assets.

Cinema | Generate larger cinematic sequences or campaign-level creative when appropriate; not required for every episode.

Edit | Episode timeline, assembly, reframing, captions, color/finishing and derivatives.

Asset Library | Single source of stored media/documents and rights metadata.

Review | Shared comments/approvals/version comparison.

QC | Shared technical QC plus Vertical Drama heuristic continuity checks.

Delivery | Shared profile-driven packaging with vertical-drama metadata.

AI Copilot | Can answer “Which episodes are blocked?”, “What canon conflicts exist?”, “How much did Season 1 cost?” using project context.



--- TABLE 34 ---

NON-NEGOTIABLE Kurdish Sorani must be implemented as a first-class locale (ckb-IQ), not as an after-launch translation. The entire IP development and episode-production workflow must work with Kurdish titles, scripts, dialogue, metadata, subtitles, filenames and exports.



--- TABLE 35 ---

Requirement | Implementation

Locale | Use ckb-IQ in user/project/content locale fields.

Direction | RTL at correct layout root; local LTR islands for timecode, URLs, model keys, file names, lens/fps values.

Unicode | UTF-8 end-to-end; preserve authored display text.

Search | Derived normalized search aliases for common Arabic/Kurdish letter variants; do not overwrite stored names.

Screenplay | Structured elements; mixed INT./EXT., numbers and Kurdish scene text must render correctly.

Tables/grids | Descriptive cells RTL; numeric/cost/timecode columns may remain LTR.

Subtitles | Correct shaping, punctuation, line breaks, cue timing and preview.

TTS/dubbing | Pronunciation dictionary for Kurdish names/places.

Exports | PDF/DOCX/CSV/metadata must preserve Kurdish glyph joining and RTL.

UI strings | All externalized localization keys; no hard-coded English in ckb-IQ UI except approved brand/industry tokens.



--- TABLE 36 ---

Role | Typical permissions

Workspace Owner | All settings, billing, policy, export/delete, role assignment.

Executive Producer / Producer | IP/season/episode approvals, spend limits, delivery, rights review according to policy.

Showrunner | Story bible, season arc, scripts, canon and continuity approvals.

Writer | Draft concept/bible/scripts; cannot lock/retcon unless granted.

Director | Visual bible, shot plans, selections, picture review.

AI Artist / Operator | Generate assets within assigned episodes/limits; cannot approve rights or master.

Editor | Edit timelines, versions, picture-lock proposal.

Localization Lead | Translations/dubs/localization approval for assigned languages.

QC Reviewer | Run/review QC, configured overrides.

Rights/IP Manager | Rights records, evidence, clearance state; no creative overwrite.

Viewer/Client | Review/comment only, optional approval scope.



--- TABLE 37 ---

Cost event | Record

Text generation | tokens/units, provider/model, internal cost, user credit charge.

Image generation | candidates, resolution, steps/workflow, provider cost.

Video generation | duration/resolution/model/provider billed units and actual/estimated cost.

Voice/audio | duration/characters/provider billed units.

Private GPU | active seconds/minutes, worker/GPU class, allocation basis.

CPU processing | optional internal cost estimate for margin accounting.

Storage/egress | optional project-level internal economics.

Failed jobs | provider charge if any; user charge/refund policy explicit.



--- TABLE 38 ---

Admin area | Capabilities

Product Entitlements | Enable plans/features, approval gates, quotas.

Model Registry | Art City workflow labels, providers/models, quality tiers, fallbacks.

Provider Registry | Keys/credentials references, status, regions, policy, pricing basis.

Pricing Ledger | Dated model/GPU/credit prices; never hard-code current prices in product logic.

Prompt Registry | Versioned system prompts/templates/examples per locale.

Delivery Profiles | Codec/resolution/duration/metadata/subtitle rules per destination.

Content Policies | Allowed/rating/provider restrictions.

Localization | UI strings, terminology, Kurdish dictionary/pronunciations.

Rights Policies | Which states block generation/master/delivery.

Job Operations | Queue, retry, cancel, provider failure/fallback.

Cost Dashboard | Spend by workspace/project/series/episode/provider/model and gross-margin proxy.

Audit | Sensitive actions and admin access.



--- TABLE 39 ---

Project | Purpose

Sorani serialized drama – 10 episodes | Full ckb-IQ story bible, dialogue, RTL UI, subtitles, Kurdish filenames, mixed English technical tokens.

English romance/thriller – 10 episodes | Hook/cliffhanger/continuity and AI-native generation pipeline.

Arabic localization variant | RTL subtitle/dub/localization lineage from an English or Sorani source.

Hybrid live-action mini-series | Uses AC Script, storyboard, schedule/call sheet, dailies ingest and Art City Edit.

Character transformation arc | Multiple approved appearance variants across episodes; verifies identity continuity.

Provider failover test | Primary video provider fails; Router uses configured fallback without duplicate user charge or duplicate selected asset.



--- TABLE 40 ---

Phase | Primary deliverables | Release target

Phase 0 – Foundation | Domain package/routes; shared Project/Asset/Router integration; ckb-IQ; entitlements; core tables; rights/provenance; job/cost ledger contracts. | Architecture ready

Phase 1 – IP Development MVP | IP Vault, concept, story bible, characters, world, style lock, series/season/episode objects, episode grid. | Users can build a controlled IP/season.

Phase 2 – Episode Writing & Continuity | Beat engine, AC Script integration, hook/cliffhanger inspector, canon conflict checker, script lock/version dependencies. | Users can lock production-ready episodes.

Phase 3 – AI Production | Découpage/vertical shots, reference/identity locks, image/video generation, candidate selection, voice/dialogue, batch jobs. | Users can produce AI-native episodes.

Phase 4 – Edit / Localization / Master | Art City Edit handoff, picture lock, subtitles/dub, QC, mastering, delivery profiles. | End-to-end mastered/delivered episode.

Phase 5 – Analytics Learning | Performance import/connectors, beat mapping, future-episode recommendations, cost/performance analytics. | Factory learns from releases.

Phase 6 – Scale / Enterprise | Multi-series slate dashboards, templates, remake workflows, advanced private GPU/LoRA, organization policies, API/partner delivery. | Studio/enterprise operation.



--- TABLE 41 ---

MVP RELEASE The first commercially usable MVP should include Phases 0–3 at minimum plus basic Edit/export handoff. Without IP/bible/continuity/identity locks, the product is only a vertical video generator and does not justify the “IP Factory” positioning.



--- TABLE 42 ---

Risk / decision | Why it matters | Mitigation / required decision

Treating product as generator | No defensible workflow/IP value; continuity collapses. | Ship IP/bible/episode/canon/identity workflow as core.

Character drift | Breaks audience trust and serial continuity. | Reference locks, appearance variants, provider adapters, QA.

Provider lock-in | Prices/models/availability change. | Shared Router + provider abstraction + registry.

AI cost explosion | Large seasons multiply failed candidates. | Preflight cost, batch caps, acceptance-rate metrics, private GPU where economic.

Rights ambiguity | Can block distribution/partnerships. | IP Vault, source declaration, releases/licenses, human review.

AI authorship uncertainty | Jurisdiction-specific protection may depend on human contribution. | Contribution ledger, human approvals/revisions; legal review outside product.

Canon drift | Batch LLM generation invents contradictions. | Approved snapshots, structured canon facts, continuity checks.

Over-automation | Mass generation before creative approval wastes money. | Approval gates before expensive stages.

Kurdish treated late | RTL/script/TTS issues become architectural rework. | ckb-IQ from Phase 0 with golden fixtures.

Analytics overclaim | Correlation can be misrepresented as creative certainty. | Confidence/limitations; experiment recommendations only.

Separate platform duplication | Splits assets/accounts/billing and increases maintenance. | Separate domain, shared Art City core.

Monolithic coupling | Future scale difficult if domain boundaries are unclear. | Modular package/interfaces/event contracts; extract services later only when justified.



--- TABLE 43 ---

Workflow key | Purpose

vd.concept.generate | Structured concept alternatives.

vd.bible.generate | Story Bible proposal.

vd.season.arc.generate | Season arc.

vd.season.episode_grid.generate | Episode grid.

vd.episode.beats.generate | Beat sheet.

vd.episode.script.generate | Episode screenplay draft.

vd.continuity.check | Canon/continuity analysis.

vd.character.reference.generate | Character/reference sheet.

vd.location.reference.generate | World/location look frames.

vd.storyboard.frame.generate | Storyboard frames.

vd.shot.video.generate.standard | Standard vertical video generation.

vd.shot.video.generate.premium | Premium vertical video generation.

vd.voice.take.generate | Dialogue voice take.

vd.localization.translate | Translation.

vd.localization.dub | Dub/voice generation.

vd.localization.lipsync | Optional lip-sync.

vd.qc.continuity | Heuristic visual/narrative continuity checks.

vd.analytics.recommend | Future-episode performance recommendations.



--- TABLE 44 ---

BUILD PRINCIPLE Art City AI Vertical Drama IP Factory is not a new island and not a feature hidden inside Studio. Build it as a first-class Art City AI product domain with its own serial storytelling and IP-control intelligence, connected to the same Project, Assets, AI Router, production modules, Edit, QC, Delivery, permissions and cost infrastructure.
docs/STAGING_AND_DEPLOY.md
# Staging and deploy controls



## Environments



| Environment | Purpose |

|-------------|---------|

| development | Local Docker + uvicorn |

| staging | Railway `staging` environment — separate Postgres/Redis/MinIO vars |

| production | Railway `production` — deploy from `main` only |



## Railway staging



1. In the Art City Railway project, create environment `staging`.

2. Duplicate Postgres / Redis / MinIO (or add new plugins) into staging.

3. Set per-environment variables:

   - `SECRET_KEY` (unique)

   - `CORS_ORIGINS` (staging frontend URL)

   - `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL` (staging API URL)

   - `EXTERNAL_PROVIDERS_ENABLED=true|false`

   - `AUTH_REQUIRED=true`

4. Deploy backend/frontend into `staging` before promoting to production.



## GitHub



- Protect `main`: PR required, ≥1 reviewer, no force push

- CI: `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (pytest + Next lint/build)

- Never commit `.env`, datasets, or model weights



## Branch flow



`feature/*` → `development` → `staging` → `main`

frontend/Dockerfile
FROM node:20-alpine AS deps

WORKDIR /app

COPY package.json package-lock.json* ./

RUN npm ci



FROM node:20-alpine AS builder

WORKDIR /app

COPY --from=deps /app/node_modules ./node_modules

COPY . .

ARG NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL

ENV NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL=$NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL

RUN npm run build



FROM node:20-alpine AS runner

WORKDIR /app

ENV NODE_ENV=production

ENV HOSTNAME=0.0.0.0

ENV PORT=3000



RUN addgroup --system --gid 1001 nodejs && adduser --system --uid 1001 nextjs



COPY --from=builder /app/public ./public

COPY --from=builder --chown=nextjs:nodejs /app/.next/standalone ./

COPY --from=builder --chown=nextjs:nodejs /app/.next/static ./.next/static



USER nextjs

EXPOSE 3000

CMD ["node", "server.js"]
